items.case: Association for Democratic Reforms & Ors. v. Election Commission of India, W.P.(C) No. 640 of 2025 and connected petitions

items.quote: We deem it appropriate to clarify that certain petitions (for instance, Writ Petition (Civil) No. 855 of 2025) have in fact been instituted in support of the SIR exercise. The Petitioner(s) in these cases have urged that such an exercise ought to be conducted at regular intervals to prevent and curb the inclusion of ineligible persons in the electoral rolls on account of illegal influx.

items.case: Association for Democratic Reforms & Ors. v. Election Commission of India, W.P.(C) No. 640 of 2025 and connected petitions
items.headline: The Supreme Court upholds the Bihar revision
items.claim: The Court held the Bihar revision lawful under section 21(3) of the Representation of the People Act read with Article 324 and said declining to enrol someone does not declare that person not to be a citizen.
items.quote: It does not amount to a declaration that the individual is not a citizen of India; it merely reflects the Commission’s inability to be satisfied, for electoral purposes, that the statutory conditions are met.

items.outlet: Delhi High Court (order of 14.10.2026, as published by LiveLaw)
items.case: W.P.(C) 14955/2026, a petition by two electors, Delhi High Court
items.headline: Delhi High Court closes a petition by two electors left off the roll and leaves them free to file Form 6
items.claim: The Delhi High Court closed a petition by two electors whose names were left off Delhi's roll after they moved house and could not fill the enumeration form. They had asked the Court to quash para 4(c) of the SIR guidelines and to change the procedure that requires such electors to seek fresh inclusion through Form 6, and to restore their entries and let them move them to their new address through Form 8. The Commission's standing counsel said they could file Form 6 and that the Electoral Registration Officer would help. The first petitioner said that filing Form 6 would be a false declaration. The bench said that, since the suggestion came from the Commission's counsel on the officer's instructions, his fear of being accused of a false declaration was misplaced. It closed the petition and said the petitioners could file Form 6 if they wished, to be processed in accordance with law. It did not decide the challenge to the guidelines.
items.quote: Having heard learned counsel for the parties, we are of the considered opinion that when the suggestion is coming from the learned standing counsel appearing for ECI, that too as per the instructions of the Electoral Registration Officer, petitioner no.1’s apprehension that he would be accused of furnishing a false declaration is misplaced. ... With these observations, the writ proceedings are closed. Petitioners, if so desire, may fill Form 6, which shall be processed in accordance with law.
items.response: The Commission's standing counsel said the grievance could be redressed if the petitioners filed Form 6 under rule 25(2) read with rule 13(1)(a) of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, and that he had asked the first petitioner to do so at the previous hearing and the Electoral Registration Officer would help.

items.case: PIL on homeless and demolition-displaced voters, Delhi High Court
items.headline: Delhi SIR: plea to include homeless and demolition-displaced voters
items.claim: A PIL asked the Delhi High Court for special arrangements so homeless and displaced people could enrol in the revision, and the Court reserved its order and said it would not monitor the policy, LiveLaw reported. LiveLaw reported on 1 September that the bench of Chief Justice D.K. Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia had dismissed the petition. The Court said the Commission's Manual on Electoral Rolls already provides, in clause 8.5, how a homeless person's ordinary residence is determined, so the fear that homeless people would be left off the draft appeared to be without basis. It said any elector left off the roll after a demolition or relocation can file Form 6.
items.quote: everything cannot be thrust upon courts
items.response: The Court said the petition gave no particulars or numbers of people displaced by demolitions who remained off the roll. The Commission told the Court that clause 8.5 lets homeless people enrol without documentary proof of residence once a booth level officer has verified over more than one night that they are present at the address given, Bar and Bench reported.

items.case: Writ Petition No. 732 of 2026, a family's petition on deletion after Form 8, Bombay High Court at Goa
items.headline: 'No Business Asking Them to Fill Form 6 Because System Didn't Allow Form 8': Bombay HC Condemns ECI's Handling of SIR Process
items.claim: A family of six told the court that they had moved house within the same constituency and filed Form 8 on a BLO's instruction, and that they were then deleted from the roll because the ERONET software found no record of their cards and allowed only a rejection. The bench asked the Commission to show where the law allows a deletion without a hearing and said the family should not have been asked to file Form 6, The Wire reported, citing The Times of India.
items.quote: Questioning the legality of the removal of the Santa Cruz family from the voter list without a hearing, the bench noted, "Show us from the Act where it empowers you to delete without hearing. If you are planning to remove someone's name, you have to give the person an opportunity of hearing first." ... According to TOI, the bench replied, "You have no business asking them to fill Form 6 because the system didn't allow you to do it on Form 8. That was the problem."
items.response: The Wire reported that the Commission's counsel said other voters deleted in the same way had been put back on the roll after filing Form 6, and that the family had not filed Form 6 when asked to.

items.case: W.P.(Crl.) No. 401 of 2026, against decisions of the Chief Election Commissioner, Supreme Court

items.quote: Any modified Form 6 has not been approved by us. Let's be clear.

items.case: Writ Petition No. 732 of 2026, a family's petition on deletion after Form 8, Bombay High Court at Goa
items.headline: 'What Is SIR's Purpose If Citizens Are Being Removed From Voter's List? Bombay High Court Asks ECI
items.claim: At a further hearing of the same family's petition the bench asked what purpose the revision served if citizens were left off the roll. It also asked why a voter who had moved house should have to sign the enumeration form, whose declaration says the voter still lives at the address on the existing roll, LiveLaw reported.
items.quote: "Read the judgment, it says ECI has an obligation to ensure that all Indian citizens are on the list... If citizens are excluded what will we do with your SIR? If citizens are being removed from the list then what is the purpose of this entire SIR process then?" ... "If a voter comes to you with Form 8, saying he has changed his address you just cannot tell that person that look your name isn't included in the draft roll now you will have to fill in Form 6 (inclusion of new voter). Your enumeration form, basically has a declaration that a person continues to live in the address as mentioned in the existing voters list. But consider, if someone has changed their residence, can you compel the person to make a false declaration by submitting that pre-filled enumeration? Why can't that person simply give a Form 8 because anyway, his name is there in the existing list he just wants to get his address changed.. Why compel enumeration form?" Justice Menezes observed.
items.response: LiveLaw reported that the Commission's counsel argued that a voter had to submit the enumeration form along with Form 8 to have an address changed, and that a voter who did not submit it had to file Form 6.

items.case: Petition on the implementation of the SIR in Maharashtra, Bombay High Court
items.headline: Maharashtra SIR: Bombay High Court Declines Oral Plea To Restrain ECI From Deleting Voters' Names, Says SC Seized Of Issue
items.claim: The Chief Justice's bench refused an oral request to order that no names be deleted from the roll in Maharashtra for the time being. It said it would follow the Supreme Court, which it was told had restrained High Courts in November 2025 from hearing petitions on the revision, and adjourned the case by four weeks, LiveLaw reported. The petition asks for the order and reasons behind the revision in the state and for safeguards against wrongful exclusion.
items.quote: "There are restraining orders already... No purpose will be served by a parallel litigation. Let the SC hear the matter first and we will consider it later," Chief Justice said. ... The judges turned down the said oral prayer, by observing, "No no no...we are not going to pass any such orders... We will follow judicial propriety." The bench accordingly, adjourned the hearing for four weeks.

items.case: WP 32975 of 2026, a petition by two electors, Telangana High Court
items.headline: Telangana SIR | Plea Challenges 'AI-Based' SIR Process; High Court Asks ECI Why Voter Was Excluded Without Notice
items.claim: The Telangana High Court asked the Commission why one petitioner was left off the roll without a notice and what happened to the other after his hearing, LiveLaw reported. The petition challenges notices over minor discrepancies and the automated matching used in the revision. The case was listed again for 13 October. At the hearing of 13 October, senior counsel for the Commission said one petitioner's name had been deleted and he would have to file Form 6, and that the other's petition was premature because the final roll had not been published, Telangana Today reported. He assured the bench that reasoned orders, open to appeal, would be passed where electors on the draft were left off the final roll, provided they attended the hearings on their notices and gave documents. He said that where no order was passed, the elector's name could be taken as included. The case was adjourned to 15 October.
items.quote: If he has satisfied and explained on the mismatch, you must have taken a decision on that,
items.response: The Commission's counsel sought time for instructions. She said the second petitioner was sent a notice over a mismatch in his father's name and heard on 15 September, and that the first could file Form 6.

items.case: Writ Petition No. 732 of 2026, a family's petition on deletion after Form 8, Bombay High Court at Goa
items.headline: Goa HC adjourns hearing on plea challenging voter deletion as ECI points out SC cases
items.claim: The Bombay High Court at Goa adjourned the St Cruz family's petition by a week at the Commission's request, after the Commission said orders the Supreme Court might pass could bear on it. items.case: Application by five deleted electors in the West Bengal SIR matter, Supreme Court
items.headline: SIR-Deleted Voters Move Supreme Court For Expeditious Disposal Of Appeals Before Kolkata, Howrah Municipal Elections

items.case: MA Baby v. Union of India and others, WP(c) 63560/2026, Supreme Court
items.headline: Don't Completely Stop Trains/Metro In Delhi To Handle October 10 Protests : Supreme Court To Centre
items.claim: The Supreme Court told the Centre not to stop all trains and Metro services in Delhi before the 10 October protests against the Chief Election Commissioner, and to run them in a regulated way, LiveLaw reported. The petition was brought by CPI(M) General Secretary MA Baby and others against the closure of 57 Metro stations and the cancellation of trains due at New Delhi and Nizamuddin. The order said the notifications appeared to be overreaching, and ETV Bharat reported that the bench also asked the Centre to reconsider Jantar Mantar as the designated protest site.
items.quote: there shall be no outright prohibition on the movement of Metro trains
items.response: The order records that the Solicitor General "has fairly agreed to impress upon the authorities to reassess such prohibitions." He said the impression that the whole city had been shut "is far from the truth."

items.case: Application by five deleted electors in the West Bengal SIR matter, Supreme Court
items.headline: 'We Are Conscious' : Supreme Court To Consider Plea To Prioritise SIR-Deleted Voters' Appeals Ahead Of Kolkata, Howrah Municipal Elections
items.claim: Counsel for electors deleted from West Bengal's roll after adjudication asked the Supreme Court to hear their plea before the Kolkata and Howrah municipal elections and to let appellants vote, LiveLaw reported. The Chief Justice said the Court would try to list it on 16 October, or else on 29 October, and suggested the tribunals take up appeals for inclusion first and appeals seeking deletion last. Counsel told the Court that nearly 1.70 lakh appeals from the two municipal areas were pending.
items.quote: We will find out if we can list on 16th (Friday) ...otherwise 29th is best way.
items.response: No submission by the Commission was reported. The figures put to the Court were counsel's, partly drawn from the Commission's affidavits.

items.case: Paka Suresh v. Union of India, SLP(C) No. 35786/2026, Supreme Court
items.headline: Andhra Pradesh Local Body Elections | Conduct Polls As Per Old Rolls If SIR Not Complete Before Notification: Supreme Court
items.claim: The Supreme Court, hearing a challenge to the Andhra Pradesh High Court's order for local body elections within six weeks, said the elections should use the revised roll if it is published before the polls are notified, and the existing roll if it is not. It said the roll in force applies until the Commission publishes the revised list and that the revision cannot be a reason to delay the polls.
items.quote: However, if the final SIR rolls were not published before the notification, the elections would be conducted using the existing electoral rolls in accordance with the applicable State laws.
items.response: The bench noted that the Election Commission had proposed to publish the final roll on 16 October 2026. Senior counsel for the State Election Commission said the rolls in force continue until the Commission publishes a fresh list. Deccan Chronicle reported on 15 October that the Commission had moved the final publication in Andhra Pradesh to 30 October and the last date for disposing of claims and objections to 22 October. The Wire reported that the YSRCP moved the Supreme Court on 20 October, alleging that violence during the filing of nominations for the state's urban local body elections kept its candidates from taking part.

items.case: Contempt petition against the Union Home Secretary, the Delhi Police Commissioner and the DMRC chairperson, Supreme Court
items.headline: Supreme Court Contempt Plea Alleges Delhi Authorities Defied Order On Metro, Train Curbs
items.claim: A contempt plea filed in the Supreme Court on 10 October alleged that the Centre and Delhi authorities defied the Court's order of 9 October, keeping 57 Metro stations shut and cancelling Delhi-bound trains before the protest against the Chief Election Commissioner, Outlook reported. The plea also said no traffic advisory had been published in newspapers. A bench of Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana listed it to be heard with a petition against the detention of opposition leaders at a special sitting on Sunday 11 October, Bar and Bench reported. On 15 October, before the Chief Justice and Justice Bagchi, the Delhi Police Commissioner filed two affidavits that tendered an unconditional apology for any perceived non-compliance and said there had been no non-compliance with the Court's orders of 9 and 11 October. Justice Bagchi observed that on the Solicitor General's account the apology appeared qualified.
items.quote: "Notwithstanding the solemn judicial mandate and the assurance recorded before the bench of the Chief Justice of India (CJI), the contemnors have consciously maintained a blanket shutdown across transit corridors, persisted with unwarranted train cancellations, and failed to issue or publicize transparent traffic and transit advisories."
items.response: The Solicitor General said the apology was included as standard practice in answering a contempt notice and that the government was defending its actions on facts. The Commissioner asked for the contempt notice to be discharged.

items.case: Rahul Gandhi v. Election Commission of India, W.P.(C) No. 1351 of 2026 (Diary No. 64196 of 2026), Supreme Court
items.headline: SC registry points out 10 defects in Rahul Gandhi's plea in SIR case
items.claim: Rahul Gandhi, Mallikarjun Kharge and other INDIA bloc leaders filed a writ petition in the Supreme Court on 12 October against the Election Commission, the Chief Election Commissioner and the two Election Commissioners. Delhi Police stopped their march to the Court on Bhagwant Das Road, and counsel filed the petition shortly before the filing counter closed. LiveLaw reported that the leaders then went to the Registry, and that a large crowd gathered inside the Court's precincts. The petition asks for the SIR to be suspended in every state while the case is heard, for a committee under a retired Supreme Court judge to audit the names left off or deleted, and for the Commission's files on its decision to hold the revision. PTI reported that the Registry flagged more than ten defects in it, among them illegible or missing pages, an unclear copy of Kharge's identity card and a court fee short by over Rs 200. LawBeat reported that the Registry registered it on 13 October once the defects were cured.
items.quote: Besides, the registry also pointed out a shortfall of over Rs 200 in court fee.
items.response: No response from the Commission was reported.

items.case: A fresh writ petition on the modified Form 6, Supreme Court (petitioner not reported)
items.headline: We have neither approved nor disapproved ECI's Form 6 modification: Supreme Court clarifies
items.claim: On a fresh writ petition, the bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana said its remarks of 5 October meant only that the modified Form 6 did not exist when the Bihar case was heard, and that the Court had neither approved nor disapproved it, Bar and Bench reported. Counsel for the petitioner had said the Commission was presenting the altered form as approved by the Court. The Hindustan Times reported that the bench said it would examine the issue and listed the petition with the batch of SIR petitions on 27 October, when it would also take up the wider challenge to how the Commission's decisions on the revision were taken.
items.quote: What was said was that when the Bihar SIR matter was before us, the new Form 6 was not there. That does not mean it was either approved or disapproved by the Supreme Court
items.response: The Commission's press note of 26 September said the Supreme Court had upheld the additional declaration attached to Form 6 for the revision. The Hindustan Times reported that the Commission maintains the statutory form itself was not altered and that the declaration is an addendum for the revision only.

items.case: Application by two transparency activists in their pending petition on the Delhi SIR, W.P.(C) No. 1188 of 2026, Supreme Court
items.headline: Delhi SIR: Supreme Court Advances Hearing After Plea Flags Deleted Voters Being Asked To Fill Form 6
items.claim: Two transparency activists who had petitioned the Court on the Delhi revision filed an application against the requirement that electors left off Delhi's draft apply again on Form 6, whose declaration says the applicant is applying for inclusion for the first time, LiveLaw reported. The application says 47,56,722 electors, 32.78% of those on the roll before the revision, were left off the draft, and that a false declaration can be punished under section 31 of the 1950 Act. It asks for a way to restore these electors without that declaration, and for the additional declaration form added to Forms 6 and 8 through the SIR guidelines to be declared without the force of law because it was not made under section 28 of the Act. Counsel asked the Court to let them use Form 8 or another form. On 14 October the bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi moved the hearing of the main petition from 30 to 28 October.
items.quote: we are thinking of passing an order that will take care of [all this]
items.response: No submission by the Commission was reported. Counsel told the Court that 30 October was the last date in Delhi for correcting deletions.

items.case: Rahul Gandhi v. Election Commission of India, W.P.(C) No. 1351 of 2026 (Diary No. 64196 of 2026), Supreme Court
items.headline: 'One Petitioner Has To Explain His Conduct': Supreme Court Issues Notice On INDIA Bloc Leaders' Petition Against ECI Over SIR
items.claim: A bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi issued notice on the INDIA bloc leaders' petition to the Election Commission, Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, LiveLaw reported. Bar and Bench reported that the bench tagged it with the SIR cases already pending. The Chief Justice said that issuing notice did not mean the Court was condemning anything, and that the Court would ask one of the petitioners about his conduct at the next hearing. He said the petition would be entertained on that petitioner's behalf on a provisional basis, subject to his explaining his conduct. The bench did not name him in court. LiveLaw reported that the written order, uploaded later that day, names him as petitioner no. 6, Shiv Sena (UBT) leader and Rajya Sabha MP Sanjay Raut. Notice was also issued on separate petitions by AIMIM president Asaduddin Owaisi and Congress leader Digvijaya Singh. No interim order was reported. The Hindustan Times had reported on 12 October that the batch of SIR petitions was listed for 27 October.
items.quote: "We would also ask one of the petitioners about his conduct."
items.response: No counsel for the Commission was reported. The Court said "Somebody will accept notice on behalf of the Election Commission of India," Bar and Bench reported.

items.case: W.P.(C) No. 1360 of 2026 (Diary No. 64394 of 2026), a petition by four advocates on the march of 12 October, Supreme Court
items.headline: 'Nobody Can Browbeat Us' : Supreme Court In Plea Against October 12 March By Opposition Leaders; Issues Notice
items.claim: The same bench issued notice on a petition by four advocates about the INDIA bloc's march to the Supreme Court on 12 October, and on a second plea seeking similar relief, LiveLaw reported. The petition asks for rules on demonstrations near the Supreme Court and the High Courts and for criminal contempt proceedings against Rahul Gandhi, Mallikarjun Kharge, Akhilesh Yadav and Mahua Moitra. Senior counsel for the petitioners said about 200 lawyers had signed a memorandum calling the march browbeating. The Chief Justice said nobody could browbeat the Court and that the judges knew what was said outside it. The Court directed all law enforcement agencies to preserve the CCTV footage and other digital material they had collected, and LiveLaw reported that it also directed footage of the Court's premises to be preserved. Bar and Bench reported that notice went to the Congress, Rahul Gandhi and other INDIA bloc leaders, and that the Court declined to begin contempt proceedings that day.
items.quote: "Nobody can browbeat us," the CJI responded. ... "We are not sitting in ivory towers." "We know what statements they make outside and what they say in Court."
items.response: No reply from the leaders named was reported.

items.case: Plea on voter deletions in Maharashtra's SIR, Supreme Court (petitioner and case number not reported)
items.headline: Supreme Court Lists Maharashtra SIR Voter Deletions Plea For October 26, Says Matters Cannot Be Generalised
items.claim: The Supreme Court declined to issue notice on 15 October on a plea about deletions in Maharashtra's revision and listed it for 26 October, LawChakra reported. The Chief Justice refused to hear it with the other petitions on the revision and said the Court would take the states one at a time, Maharashtra first and then Delhi. The petition says about 1.2 crore of Maharashtra's 9.79 crore electors were flagged for logical discrepancies, and the Commission had not yet replied. Bar and Bench reported that senior counsel for the petitioner, Arvind Datar, told the Court that 1.2 crore of Maharashtra's 9.79 crore electors had been flagged for logical discrepancies and that 40.6% of electors had been left off the roll in Pune and some other areas. He asked for notice to be issued that day so that the authorities could reply before 26 October, and the Chief Justice said "Not today. Not today."
items.quote: This cannot be generalised. We have to look at it state-wise.
items.response: LawChakra reported that the Election Commission's response was not yet on record. Maharashtra's period for claims and objections ran to 26 October, the day of the hearing.

items.case: Appeals by the Election Commission before West Bengal's SIR appellate tribunals
items.headline: Election Commission Seeks to Remove Half the Bengal Voters Judges Have Cleared For Inclusion
items.claim: The Election Commission had filed appeals before West Bengal's SIR appellate tribunals against the inclusion of at least 14,75,887 voters by 17 October, 49.2% of the 30,00,545 voters in the records whom judicial officers had examined and found eligible, The Wire reported from appeal records collected by the Civic Research Group. Malda, Murshidabad and Uttar Dinajpur hold 44.6% of these appeals. In the 41 seats where minorities are more than half the population the appeals equal 5.9% of the draft roll, and in the 89 seats where they are under 10% they equal 0.6%. The tribunals had decided 80,091 appeals, or 5.4%, and the report says no tribunal has been able to upload an order since 21 September. In a follow-up on 24 October, The Wire reported that the Civic Research Group's fuller records show 16,08,175 appeals by the Commission against 32,53,401 voters found eligible, 49.4%, close to the 16,10,311 appeals against inclusion that the Commission reported to the Supreme Court in September. It reported that the appeal numbers carry a filing date, a structure that activists found and The Wire says it verified, and that 13,85,374 of the 13,95,794 appeal IDs in an earlier extract of 17 October, or 99.3%, carry one of three dates, 5, 6 or 8 April 2026, with more than 12 lakh on 5 April. The roll was frozen for the Assembly election at midnight on 7 April.
items.quote: The Commission has not disclosed on what grounds it is challenging these voters, and who exactly decided to file the appeals.
items.response: The report says the Commission has not said on what grounds it filed the appeals, who decided to file them, or whether each case was reviewed before an appeal was filed. The follow-up says only the Commission can confirm the dates read from the appeal numbers, and that a single date on more than 12 lakh appeals does not by itself show who authorised them.

items.case: PIL by an advocate for an expert committee on the Election Commission, Supreme Court
items.headline: Plea before Supreme Court seeks expert committee headed by former CJI to examine ECI's functioning
items.claim: An advocate filed a PIL in the Supreme Court asking for an independent expert committee, chaired by a former Chief Justice or judge of the Court, to examine shortcomings in the functioning of the Election Commission, Bar and Bench reported. It relies on The Indian Express report of 23 September that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi recorded written objections at least 14 times over ten months to decisions taken by Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar alone. Citing reports of a Commission affidavit, it says about 38.20 lakh appeals had been filed in West Bengal by people excluded from the roll and about 1.02 lakh decided. It also asks the Commission to bar campaigning on religious tags, religious symbols and communal appeals. No hearing date was reported.
items.quote: The petition states that it is intended to be non-partisan and prospective and that the petitioner is not seeking a finding against any political party or office-holder, nor does it challenge the result of any election.
items.response: The plea says the Commission acknowledged the dissenting notes and described them as routine suggestions. The plea describes all the West Bengal appeals as filed by people excluded from the roll. The Commission's own count splits them into 22,21,118 appeals by people found not eligible and 16,10,311 appeals against inclusion.

items.case: W.P.(C) No. 1330 of 2026, a petition on voter deletions in Maharashtra's SIR, Supreme Court
items.headline: Supreme Court assures no deleted voters will be prosecuted for submitting Form 6
items.claim: The Supreme Court issued notice to the Election Commission on 26 October on a petition against deletions in Maharashtra's revision and listed it for 5 November, and the Chief Justice orally assured that no elector deleted in the revision would be prosecuted for applying again through Form 6, The Hindu and LawChakra reported. The Bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana declined to extend the period for claims and objections, which closed that day, or to stop the final roll before hearing the Commission. Senior advocate Arvind Datar, for the petitioner, said thousands of electors in Mumbai and Pune were marked absent and then deleted because their old buildings were being redeveloped and they had moved out, and he put the redevelopment projects at 3,500 in Mumbai and 1,500 in Pune. He said electors who had been deleted were being made to file Form 6 as new voters, which he said is an offence, and asked for a new form to be notified for electors deleted in the revision. LawChakra reported that he also said about 3 crore of the state's roughly 9 crore electors had been deleted after the draft, 1.22 crore of them for a logical discrepancy, and that about 40% were missing from the rolls in Pune and Mumbai. ANI reported the Chief Justice as saying the Court could extend the date later if it found people who had yet to file their documents.
items.quote: “Do not worry. Nobody will be prosecuted,” Chief Justice Kant responded orally.
items.response: The Commission's reply is awaited. LawChakra says the Court recorded no finding on the petitioner's figures. The assurance on Form 6 was given orally in court.

items.headline: Jharkhand Assembly passes resolution against SIR
items.claim: The Week, carrying a PTI report, said the Jharkhand Assembly passed a resolution opposing the SIR, moved by Parliamentary Affairs Minister Radhakrishna Kishore on behalf of the INDIA bloc. The BJP opposed it. When a Congress member asked for a vote, the Speaker ruled that it stood passed because the ruling coalition had a majority.
items.quote: Ranchi, Aug 26 (PTI) A resolution opposing the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls was passed in the Jharkhand assembly on Tuesday. ... Replying to him, the speaker said, "The resolution stands automatically passed as the ruling coalition has a majority in the House."

items.headline: Kerala Assembly passes unanimous resolution against SIR
items.claim: The Siasat Daily, carrying a PTI report, said the Kerala Assembly unanimously passed a resolution moved by Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan against the SIR in the state, with the Congress-led opposition backing it.
items.quote: Kerala Assembly on Monday unanimously passed a resolution against the Election Commission of India (ECI)’s move to carry out the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of voters’ list in the state and urged the poll body to conduct the revision of voters’ list in a transparent manner.

items.headline: Punjab House resolution seeks probe into electoral ‘irregularities’ under CEC Gyanesh Kumar
items.claim: The Punjab Vidhan Sabha passed a resolution by voice vote on 23 October asking for an independent and impartial inquiry into alleged irregularities in voter lists, the electoral process and the functioning of the Election Commission under the Chief Election Commissioner, The Indian Express reported. The paper calls it the first resolution of its kind by an Assembly against the Chief Election Commissioner. Members of the Congress, the Shiromani Akali Dal and the BJP were not in the House when it passed. These are the resolution's and the speakers' allegations.
items.quote: This House demands establishment of an independent, impartial, and credible investigative mechanism to inquire into alleged irregularities concerning the electoral process and voter lists under Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, so that the truth can come to light and accountability can be fixed,
items.response: The report carries no response from the Commission or the BJP.

items.headline: Bandh Against SIR By INDIA Alliance Throws Life Out Of Gear In Bihar
items.claim: ETV Bharat reported that a Bihar bandh called by the INDIA bloc parties against the SIR disrupted life across much of the state, with Rahul Gandhi and Tejashwi Yadav taking part.
items.quote: Patna: The Bihar Bandh called by parties of INDIA Alliance to protest against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) before the Assembly elections, threw life out of gear in most parts of the state.

items.headline: Assembly Protest Bihar: Anti-SIR Demonstrations Disrupt Monsoon Session Opening Day
items.claim: Deccan Herald, carrying a PTI report, said opposition members protested against the SIR inside the Bihar Assembly on the first day of its monsoon session, with CPI(ML) Liberation legislators wearing black.
items.quote: Patna: Protests against special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in Bihar rocked the state assembly on the inaugural day of the monsoon session on Monday.

items.headline: Sonia, Kharge, Rahul, Akhilesh Join Opposition Leaders In Protest Against SIR
items.claim: ETV Bharat reported that INDIA bloc MPs protested at the Makar Dwar of Parliament against the Bihar SIR for a fifth day running and demanded that it be rolled back.
items.quote: Several MPs of the INDIA bloc parties, including Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge and Congress parliamentary party chairperson Sonia Gandhi, protested in the Parliament House complex on Monday against the Election Commission's voter roll revision in Bihar, and demanded its rollback.

items.headline: Police Stop March of 300 Opposition MPs Against Bihar SIR, Detain Lawmakers
items.claim: The Wire reported that Delhi Police detained opposition MPs, among them Mallikarjun Kharge and Rahul Gandhi, when their march from Parliament to the Election Commission against the Bihar SIR was stopped, and that they were released in the afternoon.
items.quote: Opposition MPs including leaders of opposition in the Rajya Sabha and Lok Sabha – Mallikarjun Kharge and Rahul Gandhi – were detained by Delhi Police today (August 11) after they were stopped during their protest march against the ‘special intensive revision’ of the voter rolls in Bihar.
items.response: The Wire reported that the Commission had written to Jairam Ramesh the day before asking for the names of 30 members for a meeting “due to limitation of space”.

items.headline: Rahul Gandhi Kicks Off 'Vote Adhikar Yatra' In Bihar To 'Protect' Electoral Rights
items.claim: ETV Bharat reported that Rahul Gandhi began a 16-day Vote Adhikar Yatra from Sasaram against the SIR in Bihar, due to end with a rally in Patna on 1 September. The Congress leader alleged that the SIR was being done to steal votes.
items.quote: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi began his ‘Vote Adhikar Yatra’ from Sasaram on Sunday, protesting against the irregularities in the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls by the Election Commission (EC) in Bihar, and with a vow to prevent anyone from stealing anyone's votes.

items.headline: Tamil Nadu all-party meeting opposes Election Commission’s voter roll revision, to move Supreme Court
items.claim: The News Minute reported that an all-party meeting chaired by Chief Minister M.K. Stalin, attended by nearly 50 parties, resolved to approach the Supreme Court against the SIR in Tamil Nadu. The AIADMK and the BJP were not invited and several other parties stayed away.
items.quote: In Tamil Nadu, an all-party meeting on November 2 by the ruling Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) and chaired by Chief Minister MK Stalin resolved to approach the Supreme Court of India against the Election Commission’s controversial Special Intensive Revision (SIR) in the state ahead of the 2026 Assembly elections.

items.headline: Mamata Leads Massive Kolkata Rally Against SIR, Vows To ‘Topple Delhi’ Over Voter List Purge
items.claim: ETV Bharat reported that Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee led a procession in Kolkata against the SIR. She called the SIR an assault on people's existence and democratic rights.
items.quote: Kolkata: Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee led a huge procession from Dr B.R. Ambedkar’s statue to Thakurbari, Constitution in hand, joined by lakhs, including Matua and other communities, to protest the Special Intensive Revision (SIR).

items.headline: DMK, Allies Protest Against SIR Revision in Tamil Nadu
items.claim: Akashvani News reported that the DMK and its alliance partners held protest demonstrations across Tamil Nadu against the SIR, with MPs, MLAs and district functionaries taking part.
items.quote: The ruling DMK and its alliance partners are holding protest demonstrations across the State against SIR exercise.

items.headline: Mamata leads anti-SIR march; EC to meet TMC leaders on Nov 28
items.claim: The Tribune reported that Mamata Banerjee led a three-km march from Bongaon to Thakurnagar in North 24 Parganas against the SIR, after addressing a rally at Bangaon.
items.quote: West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee on Tuesday led a three-km march from Bongaon's Chandpara to Matua- heartland Thakurnagar in North 24 Parganas district to protest the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in the state.
items.response: The Tribune reported that the Commission granted a five-member TMC delegation a meeting on 28 November.

items.headline: Opposition in Assam protests 'vote theft' through SR; slams Himanta, BJP
items.claim: The Siasat Daily, carrying a PTI report, said the united opposition held a protest at Chachal in Guwahati against alleged irregularities in the draft rolls of Assam's Special Revision. Assam Congress president Gaurav Gogoi accused Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma of misusing the Election Commission.
items.quote: Guwahati : The united opposition on Friday held a protest against alleged irregularities in the draft electoral rolls and “vote theft” through the Special Revision (SR) ahead of assembly elections in Assam.
items.response: The report said the Commission stated that the flagged names had not yet been deleted and would only be processed after formal applications in the claims and objections period.

items.headline: सपा ने फॉर्म-7 में धांधली का आरोप लगाया:सुल्तानपुर में मतदाता सूची से नाम हटाने के खिलाफ प्रदर्शन
items.claim: The Samajwadi Party demonstrated at the Sultanpur Collectorate on 3 February 2026 and gave the District Magistrate a memorandum for the Chief Election Commissioner, Dainik Bhaskar reported. The party alleged that pre-printed Form 7s in one handwriting were being submitted in bulk against voters from backward, Dalit and minority communities, and asked for them to be cancelled and for FIRs under section 31 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950.
items.quote: पार्टी के अनुसार, गाँवों और नगरों में 'प्री-प्रिंटेड' फॉर्म-7 थोक में जमा किए जा रहे हैं। इन फॉर्मों में एक ही लिखावट और छपे-छपाए विवरण पाए गए हैं, जो बूथ लेवल ऑफिसर (बीएलओ) के पास बड़ी संख्या में पहुँच रहे हैं।

items.headline: Citizens Protest Special Intensive Revision In Bengaluru's Freedom Park
items.claim: ETV Bharat reported that trade unions, women's groups, student bodies and Dalit and minority rights groups protested against the SIR at Freedom Park in Bengaluru under the banner My Vote, My Right, and urged the state government to take a stand.
items.quote: Bengaluru: Citizens gathered at Freedom Park in Bengaluru on Saturday to protest against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR).

items.headline: Mamata Ends Dharna Against 'Flaws' In SIR
items.claim: ETV Bharat reported that Mamata Banerjee ended her sit-in against the SIR on its fifth day after the Supreme Court ordered appellate tribunals to hear appeals against exclusions in West Bengal. She said the protest was suspended temporarily.
items.quote: Kolkata: West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee on Tuesday lifted her dharna against the "flawed SIR" on the fifth day, saying the protest was being suspended temporarily after the Supreme Court ordered the setting up of an appellate mechanism regarding the voter list revision.

items.headline: Congress Alleges Irregularities In SIR In Uttarakhand, Seeks Election Commission's Intervention
items.claim: ETV Bharat reported that a Congress delegation led by Kumari Selja staged a sit-in outside the Election Commission headquarters in Delhi over the SIR in Uttarakhand after saying it was not allowed into the premises.
items.quote: The delegation staged a sit-in outside the ECI headquarters. Later, they submitted a representation to a poll panel official, highlighting alleged discrepancies in the ongoing SIR of electoral roll in the Himalayan state.

items.headline: Congress protests against CEC Gyanesh Kumar spread across India; Gaurav Gogoi detained in Guwahati
items.claim: Business Today reported that Congress workers protested in several states demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the handling of the SIR, after The Indian Express reported objections recorded by two Election Commissioners.
items.quote: Congress workers staged protests across several parts of India on Friday, demanding the resignation and removal of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over the Election Commission’s handling of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.
items.response: Business Today reported that the Commission rejected the characterisation of these exchanges as institutional dissent and said final decisions on the SIR were unanimous.

items.headline: Congress protests against CEC Gyanesh Kumar spread across India; Gaurav Gogoi detained in Guwahati
items.claim: Business Today reported that police detained Assam Congress president and MP Gaurav Gogoi during a protest in Guwahati demanding the Chief Election Commissioner's resignation.
items.quote: In Guwahati, Assam Congress president and MP Gaurav Gogoi was detained by police while participating in a protest against Gyanesh Kumar.

items.headline: Jantar Mantar Protest Demanding Gyanesh Kumar’s Resignation Sees Mass Detentions Amid Delhi Police Crackdown
items.claim: The Quint reported that police detained protesters from civil society groups and student organisations at Jantar Mantar, among them CPI(ML) Liberation general secretary Dipankar Bhattacharya, as they demanded the Chief Election Commissioner's resignation and a rollback of the SIR.
items.quote: Several civil society groups, the All India Students’ Association ... Swaraj Party leader Yogendra Yadav, and activist Prashant Bhushan held a protest at Jantar Mantar to demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and a rollback of the SIR exercise.

items.headline: Congress workers protest against CEC in Lucknow, clash with police
items.claim: ThePrint, carrying a PTI report, said police detained Uttar Pradesh Congress president Ajay Rai and hundreds of party workers in Lucknow after they were stopped while marching to demand the Chief Election Commissioner's resignation.
items.quote: Lucknow, Sep 25 (PTI) Congress workers, demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, clashed with police here on Friday after they were stopped from marching towards the Uttar Pradesh Assembly.

items.headline: 'Gyanesh, it's done bro!': Youth Congress marches to Jantar Mantar; water cannons in Bihar, Punjab
items.claim: ThePrint, carrying an ANI report, said police used water cannons on Congress workers in Patna who were protesting against the Chief Election Commissioner as part of the party's nationwide programme over the SIR.
items.quote: In Patna, Bihar, police used water cannons to disperse Congress workers protesting against Gyanesh Kumar and demanding his resignation.
items.response: The report said the Commission described operational queries and internal feedback as part of the normal functioning of a multi-member body and said all final SIR decisions were unanimous.

items.headline: 'Gyanesh, it's done bro!': Youth Congress marches to Jantar Mantar; water cannons in Bihar, Punjab
items.claim: ThePrint, carrying an ANI report, said police used water cannons on Punjab Congress workers demonstrating in Chandigarh as part of the party's protests over the SIR.
items.quote: Similar scenes were witnessed in Punjab, where police deployed water cannons as Congress workers staged a demonstration in Chandigarh.

items.headline: HP Congress protests in Shimla; demands CEC Gyanesh Kumar's removal, arrest
items.claim: ThePrint, carrying a PTI report, said the Himachal Pradesh Congress protested outside the Election Commission office in Shimla, burned an effigy of the Chief Election Commissioner and raised slogans against the SIR.
items.quote: The Congress workers burned an effigy of Kumar, blackened the Commission’s board, and wrote “Chor Aayog” on it. They also raised slogans against the CEC and the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

items.headline: Meghalaya Cong burns Gyanesh Kumar effigy, demands his removal and arrest
items.claim: UNI reported that Congress workers in Shillong, led by state Congress president Vincent H. Pala, burned an effigy of the Chief Election Commissioner and demanded his removal amid the row over the SIR.
items.quote: Congress workers in Meghalaya burnt an effigy of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar here on Friday, demanding his immediate arrest and removal amid an ongoing row over the functioning of the Election Commission and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

items.headline: Uttarakhand Congress gheraos EC office, demands CEC's resignation
items.claim: Asianet Newsable reported that the Uttarakhand Congress marched in Dehradun, surrounded the Election Commission office and burned an effigy of the Chief Election Commissioner. The party raised concerns over how names were added and deleted and how objections were disposed of.
items.quote: The protesters marched from the Pradesh Congress office to the Secretariat, raising slogans, and later "gheraoed the Election Commission office". They also burnt an effigy of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

items.headline: Karnataka Cong protests against SIR, demands CEC Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation
items.claim: ThePrint, carrying a PTI report, said the Karnataka Congress, with Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar and former Chief Minister Siddaramaiah, protested at Freedom Park in Bengaluru against the SIR and demanded the Chief Election Commissioner's resignation.
items.quote: Bengaluru, Sep 26 (PTI) Karnataka Congress on Saturday staged a protest at Freedom Park here against the Election Commission’s SIR exercise, demanding the resignation and arrest of CEC Gyanesh Kumar.
items.response: The Election Commission, however, has asserted that its official orders, decisions and administrative directions have full legal sanction, and that differing views and observations are a normal part of deliberations within any institution.

items.headline: Gehlot, Dotasra detained during Cong protest in Jaipur over SIR row
items.claim: ThePrint, carrying a PTI report, said police used water cannons and detained former Chief Minister Ashok Gehlot and state Congress chief Govind Singh Dotasra during a march to the State Election Commission office in Jaipur over alleged SIR irregularities.
items.quote: Jaipur, Sep 28 (PTI) Former chief minister Ashok Gehlot and Rajasthan Congress chief Govind Singh Dotasra were among senior party leaders detained by police during a protest march to the State Election Commission office here on Monday over alleged vote theft and irregularities in SIR.

items.headline: ‘EC Played Like a Puppet’: INDIA Bloc Seals Roadmap to Ramp Up Anti-SIR Agitation
items.claim: Leaders of the INDIA bloc, 33 of them from 19 parties, agreed a plan of district marches from 2 to 8 October, a march of opposition MPs to the Commission on 6 October, a meeting with the President in the second week of October and five rallies including one in Delhi on 1 November, The Wire reported. Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge said the Commission was being used as a puppet by the Prime Minister and the Home Minister.
items.quote: The leaders' six-point action plan included "Save Democracy" marches at the district level from October 2-8, opposition MPs march to the Election Commission on October 6, a meeting with the President in the second week of October, five major rallies by the opposition including a major rally in New Delhi on November 1 as well as an appeal for the early resolution of all cases relating to the SIR and electoral matters pending before the Supreme Court.

items.headline: ‘Attempt to kill democracy’: Hyderabad civil society protests SIR, demands CEC Gyanesh Kumar's resignation
items.claim: The South First reported that more than a dozen civil society groups held a day-long protest at Dharna Chowk in Hyderabad, demanding that the SIR be scrapped and the Chief Election Commissioner resign.
items.quote: Citizens in Hyderabad gathered at Dharna Chowk on Saturday, 3 October, for a day-long protest against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

items.headline: Garjana Morcha: Uddhav, Raj Thackeray Lead Protest Seeking Gyanesh Kumar’s Resignation, Scrapping Of Maharashtra SIR
items.claim: The Free Press Journal reported that Uddhav Thackeray of the Shiv Sena (UBT) and Raj Thackeray of the MNS led the Virat Garjana Morcha in Mumbai seeking the Chief Election Commissioner's resignation. Raj Thackeray demanded that the SIR in Maharashtra be cancelled.
items.quote: Shiv Sena (UBT) chief Uddhav Thackeray and Maharashtra Navnirman Sena chief Raj Thackeray on Sunday led a protest seeking the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over allegations of irregularities in the special intensive revision process.

items.headline: Delhi Police Detain Rahul, Priyanka Gandhi During INDIA Bloc Protest Seeking CEC's Resignation
items.claim: The Wire reported that police stopped an INDIA bloc march from Parliament to the Election Commission, and that opposition MPs held a sit-in at the All India Radio building until police detained Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra that night.
items.quote: As night fell on Tuesday, October 6, opposition parties had refused to vacate the protest site until they were allowed to meet Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar and hand over their demand for his resignation.

items.headline: CEC row | EC refuses Opposition's demand for meeting
items.claim: Opposition MPs of the INDIA bloc marched from Parliament to the Commission's headquarters to press for the Chief Election Commissioner's removal, and asked for 240 MPs to meet the three Commissioners at Parliament House Annexe, Deccan Herald reported.
items.quote: "After 4.00 PM today, when the Election Commission was considering the above proposal for the...meeting with the...MPs, it was informed by the Deputy Commissioner of Police, Delhi Police, that the meeting being sought was to be held with a group of 240 MPs and that the proposed venue was the Parliament House Annexe," the EC said in a statement. The EC considered this request as "unusual and therefore, could not be accepted," as, in accordance with the protocol, such meetings are held only on the premises of the poll body. It then proposed that its "senior-most officer on duty could be sent to the meeting venue to receive the memorandum", which in itself would have been an "unprecedented step". The statement added, "however, this offer was also declined by the MPs."
items.response: The Commission said no party had sought an appointment until 4 pm, that a meeting of 240 MPs away from its premises was unusual and could not be accepted, and that the MPs declined its offer to send its senior-most officer on duty to receive their memorandum, Deccan Herald reported.

items.headline: AAP Protest: Delhi CEO office gheraoed over SIR, CEC resignation demanded
items.claim: Deccan Herald, carrying a PTI report, said AAP workers and members of other parties protested outside the Delhi Chief Electoral Officer's office demanding the Chief Election Commissioner's resignation over alleged SIR irregularities. It said AAP had earlier protested at Jantar Mantar and India Gate.
items.quote: New Delhi: Scores of AAP and other parties' workers protested outside the Delhi Chief Electoral Officer's office at Kashmere Gate on Wednesday for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

items.headline: INDIA bloc leaders march to EC office in Delhi, seek rollback of SIR
items.claim: The Tribune reported that Delhi leaders of the INDIA bloc marched to the Election Commission office and gave the Delhi Chief Electoral Officer a memorandum demanding that the SIR be cancelled and excluded eligible voters be restored. It said police detained Delhi Congress president Devender Yadav at a separate protest at Jantar Mantar.
items.quote: Delhi leaders of the INDIA bloc on Wednesday staged a protest march from Kashmiri Gate to the Election Commission (EC) office and submitted a memorandum to the Delhi Chief Electoral Officer, demanding immediate cancellation of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and restoration of names of eligible voters excluded from the draft rolls.

items.headline: INDIA bloc hands over memorandum on 'vote chori' to President Murmu, says she didn't deny charge
items.claim: An INDIA bloc delegation including Mallikarjun Kharge and Rahul Gandhi gave President Droupadi Murmu a memorandum after opposition MPs marched from Parliament House and were stopped by police at Vijay Chowk, PTI reported. Kharge said the President had asked for evidence, which the bloc would provide, and Rahul Gandhi said she had not denied what they told her and that the leaders would meet the Chief Justice on Monday. The News Mill reported that the memorandum asked for the Chief Election Commissioner's resignation, repeal of the 2023 law on the Commissioners, suspension of the SIR with the names the bloc says were left off or deleted illegally put back, a return to paper ballots, and annulment of Assembly elections of the past two years where it said evidence of vote theft had been presented. These are the INDIA bloc's demands and allegations.
items.quote: "President in no way denied what we said, she did not question what we said... she accepted our statement and sought proof of 'election chori',"
items.response: No response from Rashtrapati Bhavan or the Commission to the memorandum was reported.

items.headline: Cockroach Janta Party protest: New Delhi sealed even before the first slogan
items.claim: The South First reported on the morning of 10 October that police sealed central Delhi before the Cockroach Janta Party's protest at Jantar Mantar demanding the Chief Election Commissioner's resignation over the SIR. It said more than 1,000 people had been detained overnight and 45 Metro stations were shut, and that police detained CPI(M) leaders including Pinarayi Vijayan and John Brittas when they tried to march from Kerala House.
items.quote: "A gathering of more than four people is not allowed," a Delhi Police officer told CPM's Rajya Sabha MP John Brittas, when he tried to argue that there were only three of them. ... "This is a murder of democracy," Pinarayi told reporters.
items.response: No statement from the Commission was reported. Police told the protesters that a gathering of more than four people was not allowed.

items.case: Uday Bhanu Chib v. Union of India and Ors, Delhi High Court
items.headline: Decision to de-notify Jantar Mantar as protest site taken after Supreme Court order: Delhi police to High Court
items.claim: The Delhi Police told the Delhi High Court on 13 October that it de-notified Jantar Mantar as the designated protest site, and identified three other sites, on the basis of the Supreme Court's order of 9 October, Bar and Bench reported. That order had said suitable sites where basic amenities could be provided to protesters should be identified, and left the decision to the competent authority. The submission came on Indian Youth Congress president Uday Bhanu Chib's petition against the refusal of permission to protest at Jantar Mantar against the Chief Election Commissioner. Justice Amit Mahajan issued notice on three of its prayers, which challenge the police's reliance on its 2022 standing order and the 10-day advance notice for protests.
items.quote: The Court said appropriate sites need to be identified and designated and we have precisely done that,
items.response: The police said the petition had become infructuous because Jantar Mantar had been de-notified. On 15 October the Solicitor General told the Supreme Court that the decision followed the recommendations of a committee set up by the Union Home Ministry well before the Court's oral observations, Bar and Bench reported.

items.case: Petition by the Delhi Kirana Committee and the Delhi Iron and Hardware Merchant Association, Supreme Court
items.headline: 'If NDMC Order Disproportionate, We'll Act': Supreme Court Lists Petition Against CJP Protest After Vacation
items.claim: Counsel for two traders' associations raised in the Supreme Court on 16 October their petition against the Cockroach Janta Party's call to unfurl the tricolour in Connaught Place's Central Park that evening, saying it would obstruct trade worth Rs 200 crore a day, The Wire reported. The party had called the protest after two of its leaders were arrested for waving the flag at Jantar Mantar. The bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi said it would act on compensation if the NDMC's restrictions were found disproportionate, noted that the Delhi High Court was hearing a similar matter, and listed the petition for 26 and 27 October, after the Dussehra break.
items.quote: If we feel that the NDMC’s order is a disproportionate restriction, we told you, there is ample jurisdiction evolved by this court under compensation and public law. We will act
items.response: The Wire says the petitions appear to be concerned with the protest itself, though counsel told the Court the NDMC had shut the place by a notice the night before, as LiveLaw reported. It carries the party founder's post on X that businesses suffer when the government shuts down a city and restricts its citizens' movement.

items.headline: Students, youth activists arrested for protesting against SIR in Chennai
items.claim: Chennai police arrested students and youth activists who began a 24-hour sit-in against the revision near Rajarathinam Stadium in Egmore at 4 pm on 22 October in defiance of a police ban, The Hindu reported. Nine organisations, among them Left student and youth groups and the Cockroach Janta Party, had formed a platform called Chennai's Jantar Mantar 2.0 and asked for the Chief Election Commissioner's resignation. They were held overnight at a community hall and released the next morning at the stadium, where they resumed the protest.
items.quote: The city police on Thursday arrested students and youth activists who launched a 24-hour protest against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in defiance of a police ban.
items.response: The report carries no statement from the police beyond the ban.

items.headline: Over 150 detained in Delhi during protest against CEC Gyanesh Kumar
items.claim: Delhi Police detained more than 150 people on 23 October at a march in central Delhi against the revision and the Chief Election Commissioner, called by the Delhi Coordination Committee of People Against SIR, The Indian Express reported. About 300 people gathered near Gole Dak Khana around 2 pm and marched towards Gurdwara Bangla Sahib. When they could not reach the Commission's office they held a sit-in near the roundabout, and security forces began detaining them by 3 pm. The paper also reported that over 57 cases registered during the protests of 2 to 15 October had been moved to the Crime Branch.
items.quote: Delhi Police Friday detained more than 150 protesters during a march in Central Delhi against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.
items.response: A senior police officer said the cases were moved because they needed close technical investigation and thorough questioning.

items.headline: Keralam SIR: LDF representatives walk out of all-party meet convened by Chief Electoral Officer
items.claim: Representatives of the Left Democratic Front walked out of an all-party meeting called by Kerala's Chief Electoral Officer on 23 October for the Special Summary Revision, The Hindu reported, and asked that the names of 24.08 lakh voters left off the draft roll of the state's earlier revision be put back. The paper reports that 24.08 lakh is the fall at the draft stage and that the final roll of 21 February 2026 was 8.97 lakh below the roll of October 2025.
items.quote: The CEO expressed his helplessness. We have asked the CEO to convey the demand to the Election Commission of India (ECI),
items.response: The Chief Electoral Officer, D. Sajith Babu, said he had told the leaders he would convey to the Commission their demand that the 2 November deadline for rationalising polling stations be extended.

items.headline: Kerala BLO death sparks boycott; BLOs strike over SIR deadline stress
items.claim: The News Minute reported that hundreds of booth level officers across Kerala stayed away from SIR work on a strike call after the death of a BLO in Kannur, and that employee and teacher action councils marched to collectorates.
items.quote: A day after the death of a Booth Level Officer in Kerala’s Kannur, allegedly due Special Intensive Revision (SIR) workpressure, hundreds of Booth Level Officers (BLOs) across the state skipped work following a strike call on Monday, November 17.
items.response: The News Minute reported that Kerala's Chief Electoral Officer said he had not received any complaints regarding work pressure from BLOs.

items.headline: Tamil Nadu revenue employees association begin boycott of SIR work
items.claim: Deccan Herald, carrying a PTI report, said the Federation of Revenue Associations of Tamil Nadu began a statewide boycott of SIR work over workload, staff shortages, deadline pressure and poor training.
items.quote: Chennai: The members of the Federation of Revenue Associations of Tamil Nadu commenced their boycott of the SIR work from Tuesday, protesting against excessive workload, insufficient manpower, deadline pressure, and inadequate training.
actors: Federation of Revenue Associations of Tamil Nadu

items.headline: BLOs protest outside Bengal CEO's office over excessive work pressure, EC calls them 'real heroes'
items.claim: Deccan Herald, carrying a PTI report, said booth level officers marching under the BLO Adhikar Raksha Committee clashed with police outside the West Bengal Chief Electoral Officer's office in Kolkata over SIR workload.
items.quote: Kolkata: Alleging "excessive work pressure" and "unmanageable workload", Booth-level officers (BLOs) engaged in the ongoing SIR process in West Bengal clashed with the police on Monday while attempting to enter the Chief Electoral Officer's (CEO) office here during a demonstration, a senior officer said.
items.response: Deccan Herald reported that Chief Electoral Officer Manoj Agarwal described the BLOs as the "real heroes" of the exercise.

items.headline: ‘BLOs facing harassment in Gautam Buddha Nagar amid SIR Phase-2’: UP teachers’ body submits memorandum to DM
items.claim: The Gautam Buddh Nagar unit of the Uttar Pradesh Primary Teachers' Association wrote to the District Magistrate on 24 November 2025 alleging mental harassment of the about 1,800 teachers deployed as booth officers, two days after FIRs were registered against more than 60 booth officers and seven supervisors under section 32 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, The Indian Express reported. The association asked for the FIRs to be withdrawn and said the Commission's app did not work in rural areas.
items.quote: However, you or officials under your direction have been registering FIRs and adverse entries which is leading to the mental harassment of the teachers
items.response: The Indian Express reported that the FIRs were lodged on the orders of the District Magistrate and District Election Officer, Medha Rupam, against booth officers alleged to have shown a lack of compliance.

items.headline: Four BLOs die amid mounting pressure during electoral revision drive in UP
items.claim: After a lekhpal supervising the revision died by suicide in Bindki, Fatehpur, the Lekhpal Association protested, would not let the body be taken for post-mortem until a case was registered, and announced a boycott of SIR work unless action was taken, The New Indian Express reported.
items.quote: It also announced a boycott of SIR work from Thursday unless action was taken against those responsible for the death.

items.headline: Ahmedabad: 250 BLOs Stage Protest, Citing Threats, Pressure, Abuse and Late Night Calls
items.claim: The Wire reported that nearly 250 primary school teachers working as booth level officers stopped work and held a sit-in at a data uploading centre in Ahmedabad, alleging threats and pressure during the SIR.
items.quote: Nearly 250 primary school teachers assigned as Booth Level Officers (BLOs) halted work and held a sit-in protest on Thursday (November 27) at the data uploading centre in Khokhra, Ahmedabad, alleging “threat and pressure” during the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

items.headline: ‘Denied medical leave’, booked for ‘not signing attendance’: BLOs say UP SIR is inhumane
items.claim: Newslaundry reported that Ghaziabad registered an FIR against 21 employees for negligence in booth officer duties on 27 November 2025, after Gautam Buddh Nagar's FIRs, and that glitches in the Commission's mobile application were a main reason for slow digitisation. The Ghaziabad complainant, a deputy tehsildar, admitted the app sometimes hung. The teachers' association letter cited app glitches and repeated OTP failures.
items.quote: A key reason for lagging in the digitisation effort has been the technical glitches in the EC’s national mobile application.
items.response: Officials told Newslaundry the FIRs were for negligence. An electoral registration officer said "Those who do not work will face action." Newslaundry said it sent questions to the Uttar Pradesh Chief Electoral Officer's office.

items.headline: Up:blo की मौतों से नाराज शिक्षकों संगठनों ने खोला मोर्चा
items.claim: Amar Ujala reported that teachers' organisations in Uttar Pradesh, among them the Uttar Pradeshiya Prathmik Shikshak Sangh, objected to the deaths of teachers and staff on SIR duty and demanded jobs and compensation for their families.
items.quote: प्रदेश में विशेष गहन पुनरीक्षण अभियान में लगे शिक्षामित्रों व कर्मचारियों की मौत से शिक्षक संगठनों में काफी नाराजगी है। उनका कहना है कि उनका काम शिक्षण कार्य है, उसके बावजूद प्रशासन जबरन उनसे निर्वाचन से जुड़े कार्य कराता है।

items.case: A teacher's petition against his suspension from booth level officer duty, Punjab and Haryana High Court
items.headline: Punjab & Haryana High Court grants relief to teacher suspended for not joining SIR duty after wife's death
items.claim: The Punjab and Haryana High Court quashed the suspension of a teacher in Hisar district who had asked to be relieved of booth level officer duty after his wife died, and imposed costs of Rs 50,000 on the District Elementary Education Officer, Hisar and the Electoral Registration Officer for the Barwala constituency, Bar and Bench reported. Justice Harpreet Singh Brar found that the authorities appointed three substitutes for his booth without making sure any of them joined, and then suspended him for a duty he no longer held. The Court directed the Chief Electoral Officer, Haryana to make sure that a booth level officer who is replaced is told in writing whether he stands relieved.
items.quote: Instead of deciding his application, the respondents appointed one substitute after another without ensuring that any of them actually joined. They then held the petitioner responsible for the default of others, replaced him, and thereafter suspended him for a duty he no longer held, on an allegation of missing a training whose date they themselves cannot state
items.response: The authorities said he had never been relieved of the duty and had missed the SIR training. The Court found they could not state the date of the training, and noted that none of the three substitutes attended it either.

items.headline: Bihar Voter Roll Revision: Semi-Filled Forms Distributed to 87% Voters
items.claim: Deccan Chronicle reported the Commission saying that about 87 per cent of Bihar's 7.96 crore voters had been given semi-filled enumeration forms on the first booth officer visit.
items.quote: The Election Commission of India (ECI) on Friday said that nearly 87 per cent of the 7.96 crore voters in Bihar had been provided with semi-filled enumeration forms for the ongoing special intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

items.headline: Bihar SIR | BLOs Mass-Uploading Enumeration Forms Without Voters' Knowledge Or Consent : ADR Tells Supreme Court
items.claim: LiveLaw reported that the Association for Democratic Reforms told the Supreme Court that enumeration forms in Bihar were being uploaded by officials without voters' knowledge or consent. This is ADR's allegation in a court filing.
items.quote: "...enumeration forms are being mass-uploaded by BLOs without the knowledge or consent of the voters, in order to achieve the unrealistic target set by the ECI. Many voters have reported that their forms have been submitted online, despite never having met with any BLOs or signed any documents.
items.response: LiveLaw reported that ADR filed the rejoinder in reply to the Commission's counter-affidavit.

items.headline: Form-7 flashpoint: Bengal sees clashes, rival claims of voter roll sabotage
items.claim: National Herald reported that Trinamool workers stopped a vehicle in Khatra, Bankura said to carry thousands of pre-filled Form 7s, that police seized it and began an inquiry, and that both parties traded allegations over bulk Form 7s on the last day for filing.
items.quote: The latest confrontations follow a flashpoint last week in Bankura’s Khatra subdivision, where TMC workers intercepted a vehicle said to be carrying thousands of pre-filled Form-7s. Police seized the vehicle and began an inquiry after TMC alleged the forms were intended to erase “legitimate voters” under cover of the SIR.
items.response: National Herald reported that the BJP alleged its workers were attacked and prevented from filing forms inside government offices.

items.headline: Rajasthan SIR: BJP fraudulently removing Opposition supporters from voter lists, alleges Congress
items.claim: Scroll reported that Rajasthan Congress president Govind Singh Dotasra alleged that computer-printed Form 7s were distributed in every constituency and that booth agents' signatures were forged, and demanded a forensic inquiry. These are the Congress's allegations.
items.quote: “In every Assembly constituency, 10 thousand to 15 thousand fake computerised forms are printed,” he claimed. ... He added that several booth-level agents had given statements to the media that they had not signed these forms, and that the signatures were forged and the applications were incomplete.
items.response: Scroll reported that BJP minister Gautam Dak said a voter proposed for deletion gets time to be heard and that the Congress wanted to create a dispute.

items.headline: In Assam, ‘forged’ forms aimed at deleting thousands of Muslim voters ring alarm bells
items.claim: Scroll reported that during Assam's Special Revision a booth officer in Karimganj North was handed objections against 133 voters on forms she described as half printed and half handwritten, and that hearings were suspended in three Nagaon constituencies after complaints of fake Form 7s.
items.quote: In several Muslim-majority districts and areas of Assam, bulk objections have been filed against voters, seeking to strike their names off the electoral roll. ... In Nagaon district, the hearing process has been suspended in three Assembly constituencies after complaints of fake Form 7 applications.
items.response: Scroll quoted a senior Commission official in Guwahati saying a voter can file any number of objections but that an ERO reviews them individually when one person files more than five.

items.headline: BJP workers in Assam say their names used to seek mass voter deletion – without their knowledge
items.claim: Scroll reported that at least seven people named as objectors on Form 7s in Assam, some of them BJP booth agents and members, said they had not filed the objections.
items.quote: Scroll found at least seven people who denied having filed the complaints, even when their names, voter identity cards and phone numbers had been used in the objection forms.
items.response: Scroll quoted BJP MP Kamakhya Prasad Tasa as saying anyone can file objections and that it is for the Election Commission to take a final call.

items.headline: ‘Nothing to hide’: Assam CM says he has told BJP members to file complaints against ‘Miya’ voters
items.claim: The Indian Express reported that Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma told reporters he had told BJP members to keep filing complaints against people he called 'Miyas' and to fill Form 7s wherever possible during the Special Revision.
items.quote: I myself have told the BJP people that they should keep giving complaints against Miyas. There is nothing to hide about this. I have held meetings, I have done video conferences, and I have told people that, wherever possible, they should fill Form 7s.

items.headline: Fake Objections Filed To Delete Voter Names In Bhopal, Probe Ordered
items.claim: ETV Bharat reported that Bhopal's Collector ordered a probe after a man named as objector on Form 7s in Bhopal South-West denied filing them, and that officials found incorrect or fake objector details in several of the district's 9,037 Form 7s.
items.quote: District officials said that across seven Assembly constituencies, a total of 9,037 objections have been filed through Form 7 under the SIR process. While the number is relatively small compared to the total electorate, several cases have been found to involve incorrect or fake complainant details, prompting further scrutiny.
items.response: ETV Bharat quoted District Election Officer Kaushlendra Vikram Singh saying no one's name would be deleted without verification.

items.headline: Akhilesh Yadav flags "massive conspiracy" in SIR, questions use of pre-printed form 7 in UP villages
items.claim: The Samajwadi Party president alleged on X that pre-printed Form 7s were being distributed in villages to strike off opposition voters, that the objectors listed on them could not be traced and that signatures were forged, The Economic Times reported from ANI. He said voters from backward, Dalit and minority communities were most affected.
items.quote: Under SIR, who is distributing the pre-printed Form 7 in villages (through which someone can conspire to get another's name struck off by raising an objection)?

items.headline: Form-7’s journey from a civic chore to a political weapon
items.claim: Frontline reported that Congress general secretary K. C. Venugopal wrote to the Commission on 29 January alleging misuse of Form 7 in several states, and that the Commission said there was no limit on forms per voter but that an ERO must verify when one person files more than five.
items.quote: In the wake of the swirling controversy over Form-7, the Election Commission has clarified that there is no limit on the number of forms a voter can submit in a constituency. However, in order to prevent misuse of the facility, if more than five objections are filed by an individual, the ERO will mandatorily verify the claims.
items.response: Scroll reported on 23 January 2026 that a senior Commission official in Guwahati gave the same rule.

items.headline: सोनभद्र में मतदाता सूची से नाम हटाने की साजिश:फॉर्म 7 में झूठी आपत्तियां दर्ज कर कटवाए जा रहे नाम, जांच शुरू
items.claim: Form 7 objections were filed against 14 voters of one community in part 14 of the Sadar constituency in Sonbhadra, Dainik Bhaskar reported. The booth officer inspected on the spot and found the objections false. Two of the 14 had died and the rest were present. A Samajwadi Party district office-holder said he would take the case to the District Magistrate.
items.quote: स्थलीय निरीक्षण में इनमें से दो की मृत्यु की पुष्टि हुई, जबकि अन्य सभी मौके पर उपस्थित पाए गए।

items.headline: एसआईआर: यूपी में मतदाता सूची से नाम कटवाने वाले फ़ॉर्म 7 पर क्या है विवाद
items.claim: Residents of a village in Siddharthnagar went to the Mishrauliya police station to complain that about 86 villagers were being objected to by Form 7, BBC News Hindi reported. The booth officer told local media that one person had handed him all 86 forms, that every voter named in them was Muslim and that all of them were present.
items.quote: सभी 86 फ़ॉर्मों में जिनके नाम काटने के लिए आवेदन किया गया है वे सभी मुसलमान हैं. सभी मौजूद भी हैं. इसलिए जैसा जो भी है, मैं अपनी रिपोर्ट लगा दूंगा.
items.response: The Chief Electoral Officer told BBC News Hindi "जिन लोगों के नाम कटवाने के लिए फ़ॉर्म 7 मिला है, उन्हें नोटिस दिए बिना और सुनवाई के बगैर नाम नहीं काटे जाएंगे."

items.headline: एसआईआर: यूपी में मतदाता सूची से नाम कटवाने वाले फ़ॉर्म 7 पर क्या है विवाद
items.claim: A Samajwadi Party former minister from Gonda said more than 6,000 deletions were being sought in the Karnalganj constituency and showed BBC News Hindi printed Form 7s, one of which carried the district, polling station and constituency already filled in but no objector's name. BBC News Hindi reported that every form had 'already enrolled' ticked as the reason.
items.quote: इसके अलावा जिस कॉलम पर आपत्ति का कारण दर्ज करना होता है, सभी फ़ॉर्मों में उनमें 'पहले से नामांकित' पर टिक किया गया है.
items.response: At a press conference on 6 February the Chief Electoral Officer said "कोई भी राजनीतिक दल का कार्यकर्ता एक दिन में 10 फ़ॉर्म से ज़्यादा नहीं जमा कर सकता है. जो फ़ॉर्म 7 जमा किए गए हैं, उनकी जांच होगी. अभी कोई नाम नहीं काटे जा रहे हैं." The BJP called the Samajwadi Party's allegations baseless.

items.headline: एसआईआर: यूपी में मतदाता सूची से नाम कटवाने वाले फ़ॉर्म 7 पर क्या है विवाद
