items.claim: The Samajwadi Party MP for Badaun gave the District Magistrate a list alleging that objections were being filed to a plan, BBC News Hindi reported, including a Form 7 against an elected ward member of Kakrala who said he had been a voter since 2012. In Datganj, a BJP Assembly convener whose name was on an objection told BBC News Hindi he had signed forms the party gave him and did not personally know the voter.
items.quote: मैं बीजेपी का विधानसभा संयोजक हूं. मुझे पार्टी की तरफ़ से कुछ फ़ॉर्म मिले थे, हमने इसे साइन कर दिया
items.response: The BJP called the allegations baseless, BBC News Hindi reported, and the Commission said complaints would be examined.

items.headline: एसआईआर: यूपी में मतदाता सूची से नाम कटवाने वाले फ़ॉर्म 7 पर क्या है विवाद
items.claim: The Congress said its workers in Sant Kabir Nagar caught Form 7s being submitted to delete villagers and that the man whose signature was on them denied signing, BBC News Hindi reported. BBC News Hindi said it could not verify the video of the incident.
items.quote: इसमें जिस व्यक्ति के हस्ताक्षर थे, वह इनकार कर रहा है कि ये हस्ताक्षर उसके हैं.
items.response: The Chief Electoral Officer said "इस पर उस व्यक्ति को एफ़आईआर दर्ज करानी चाहिए जिनका हस्ताक्षर फर्ज़ी है." He said officers had been told to make sure each Form 7 was submitted by the person whose signature it carried.

items.headline: Lakhs of ‘doubtful voters’ deleted in Assam based on BJP complaints, says Himanta Sarma
items.claim: Scroll reported, citing PTI, that after Assam's final roll the Chief Minister said several deletions had been made on complaints filed by BJP workers.
items.quote: “As far as possible, our party members filed complaints,” the BJP leader said. “Names have been struck off based on these.”

items.headline: Inside the ‘organised’ attempt to delete 15,000 voters in Gujarat’s Somnath
items.claim: Newslaundry reported that the 15,663 Form 7s in Somnath were filed by 269 people, each filing 50 or more, that copies it reviewed had the voter's details printed in English and the objector's details handwritten in Gujarati, and that six of the objectors filed affidavits saying they had not filed them.
items.quote: Of the 15,663 Form-7 applications, a staggering number appeared to be pre-filled and then submitted by just 269 people. ... Newslaundry has reviewed copies of Form-7s where voter details – such as name, mobile number, constituency, EPIC number, and booth number – are printed in English, while the objectors' details are handwritten in Gujarati.
items.response: Newslaundry reported that the District Election Officer, V. N. Upadhyay, said he had deployed six AEROs to verify the objections and assured that no name would be deleted arbitrarily.

items.headline: Muslim Voter Deletion Attempts in Alwar: EC's Silence Raises Questions
items.claim: The Quint reported that thousands of Form 7s in Alwar were filed in the names of BJP booth agents, several of whom said their signatures were forged, and that no FIR or inquiry had been announced a month later.
items.quote: As per copies of forms, seen by The Quint, they were overwhelmingly filed under the names of Booth Level Agents (BLAs) working for the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and predominantly targeted Muslim voters in Rural Alwar. ... Yet no FIR, no administrative inquiry, no forensic audit of handwriting or digital origin has been announced in Alwar.
items.response: The Quint reported that calls to the District Magistrate and Sub-Divisional Magistrate for comment went unanswered.

items.headline: Form 7 controversy deepens strain on SIR 2.0
items.claim: National Herald reported that the Commission wrote to West Bengal's Chief Electoral Officer to send all Form 7 objections to EROs by 16 February and dispose of them by statutory procedure, and that it had taken cognisance of reports of Form 7 records being burnt.
items.quote: The ECI's latest communication also cited reports alleging the burning of records related to Form 7 objections in parts of West Bengal — an issue it said it had taken cognisance of.

items.headline: SIR: 544 Muslim voters marked for deletion in UP village leads to one man
items.claim: Siasat reported, citing The Indian Express, that Form 7s against 544 voters of a Shamli village were found with a booth officer, said to have been already printed with the voters' EPIC numbers, and that the District Magistrate said the forms were fake and the probe found nothing.
items.quote: The forms were allegedly already printed with Electors’ Photo Identity Card (EPIC) numbers and other personal details. In the forms, the applicant cited relocation from the village as the reason for seeking their deletion from the electoral rolls.
items.response: DM Arvind Kumar Chauhan ordered a probe and later said that the case “didn’t have any substance.” “We got an investigation done and found nothing,” he added.

items.headline: Gujarat HC notice: Probe sought into fake voter deletion pleas in SIR row
items.claim: Deccan Herald reported that the Gujarat High Court issued notice to the Commission and the state on two petitions seeking a Special Investigation Team inquiry into Form 7 objections filed during the SIR.
items.quote: The petitions have sought investigation by the Special Investigation Team. They have claimed that as part of a "larger conspiracy" thousands of illegal objection applications under form-7 were filed seeking deletion of voters' names during the recently concluded Special Intensive Revision (SIR) in the state.
items.response: Deccan Herald reported that the matter was posted for further hearing on 7 July.

items.headline: Enumeration Form 'Must' For Draft Electoral Roll
items.claim: Deccan Chronicle reported Hyderabad's District Election Officer R. V. Karnan explaining that booth officers would hand out enumeration forms already printed with each elector's details and photograph, which the elector completes and signs.
items.quote: The BLOs will carry forms already containing the elector’s photograph. Electors must paste a recent photograph, fill details and sign a declaration. BLOs will distribute forms with pre‑printed details of existing electors and guide households in filling them.

items.headline: BJP Lodges Complaint Against Officials Allegedly Favouring AIMIM
items.claim: Deccan Chronicle reported that the Telangana BJP alleged to the Chief Electoral Officer that booth officers in Hyderabad were handing enumeration forms in bulk to AIMIM leaders at party camps and letting them upload filled forms. This is the BJP's allegation.
items.quote: The BJP on Tuesday alleged that booth level officers (BLOs) were avoiding mandatory house-to-house visits in the city. Instead, they were found to be distributing enumeration forms related to ongoing SIR exercise ‘in bulk’ to AIMIM leaders at party organised camps set up in several constituencies of the Hyderabad district, the BJP alleged.

items.headline: SIR: BJP Urges CEO To Conduct Probe Into Allegations
items.claim: Deccan Chronicle reported that the BJP alleged that some booth officers in Serilingampally uploaded the blank back of enumeration forms to the Commission's app without the voter's details, and asked the Chief Electoral Officer for a probe. This is the BJP's allegation.
items.quote: Party’s State Election Commission Affairs committee chairman Marri Shashidhar Reddy alleged some BLOs have uploaded the reverse side of the Enumeration Form to the official BLO mobile application without filling in any mandatory voter details on the front side in Vivekananda Nagar division’s 575 to 580 booths.

items.headline: Form-7 misuse: Supreme Court to consider Congress MP’s plea alleging targeted deletions in U.P.
items.claim: The Hindu reported that the Supreme Court agreed to consider an application by Congress MP Tanuj Punia alleging that Form 7 objections in the Uttar Pradesh SIR were filed with false particulars, forged signatures and in the names of people who later denied filing them. The application cited one person filing objections against 32 electors in Hata, Kushinagar, and a UP Congress claim of 700 to 800 objections in four Khalilabad booths.

items.headline: Uttarakhand Congress alleges Form-7 misuse to delete voters during SIR, approaches EC
items.claim: The Pioneer reported that an Uttarakhand Congress delegation told the Chief Electoral Officer that one person had filed objections against about 6,400 voters and about 1,200 people had filed more than ten each. These are the Congress's figures.
items.quote: "Our data analysis revealed that a single individual has filed objections against the names of approximately 6,400 people. There are about 1,200 individuals who have submitted more than 10 objections each. An objection has even been filed against the name of a sitting Congress MLA," Rawat said.
items.response: The Pioneer reported that CEO V. V. R. C. Purushottam said the revision followed the rules and that observers had been sent to districts with many objections, and that Additional CEO Vijay Kumar Jogdande said an ERO must scrutinise cases where one person seeks the deletion of more than five names.

items.headline: Uttarakhand SIR: The unsolved mystery of BJP agents’ ‘forged’ objections against Muslim voters
items.claim: Newslaundry reported that 35 people named as objectors on 1,657 Form 7s in Jhabrera, 31 of them BJP booth agents, said in affidavits that their names, EPIC numbers and signatures had been misused.
items.quote: In affidavits submitted to the Haridwar district administration on August 18 and 19, each of the 35 said an “unknown person” used their name, EPIC number and a forged signature to file Form 7 applications – which are requests seeking the deletion of voters.
items.response: Newslaundry quoted the Jhabrera ERO saying the objections were cancelled after those named sought to withdraw them and the voters would not be deleted, and that the Election Commission would not order any investigation and those whose names were misused should file an FIR.

items.headline: 50,000 Forms Filed Seeking Deletion of Votes
items.claim: Deccan Chronicle reported, in a story datelined Hyderabad that does not say whether the figure covers the state or the district, that the Commission had received close to 50,000 Form 7 applications against entries in the draft roll, and that parties at a meeting chaired by Hyderabad's District Election Officer asked for the Form 10 lists by Assembly constituency.
items.quote: Amid nearly 93 lakh voters listed with logical discrepancies or placed in the absent, shifted, dead and duplicate (ASDD) list, the Election Commission of India (ECI) has received close to 50,000 Form-7 applications seeking deletion of names or raising objections to entries in the draft electoral rolls. Political parties have asked election officials to provide details of the Form-7 applications through Form 10, which is the consolidated list of objections and deletion requests received through Form 7.
items.response: Deccan Chronicle reported that officials gave parties the total number of applications at a meeting at the GHMC office but did not share figures by Assembly constituency.

items.headline: Uttarakhand SIR: Who is targeting Muslim voters?
items.claim: Newslaundry reported from its investigation in Uttarakhand that numerous applications were filed to delete Muslim voters' names from the rolls, many in the names of people it said were associated with the BJP. It reported that some people named as objectors later filed affidavits saying they had never filed the objections and that their names, EPIC numbers and signatures had been used fraudulently.

items.place: Delhi (Karol Bagh, Patel Nagar, Sangam Vihar)
items.headline: Delhi SIR: BJP Agent Files 35 Removal Requests in Two Days, ECINet Allows BLAs to Go Over 10-Claims Limit
items.claim: The Hindu reported that Form 10 lists published for 21 to 27 September showed four people in Delhi filing more than ten applications a day through the Commission's ECINET portal, which does not enforce the limit of ten a day for booth agents.
items.quote: Fresh lapses have come to light in the ongoing special intensive revision (SIR) exercise in Delhi, with official data showing that booth-level agents (BLAs) bypassed the Election Commission’s (EC) cap on submitting only 10 applications a day during the claims and objections phase by filing through the panel’s ECINET portal, which has no such restriction in place. ... The software has no mechanism to impose the prescribed limit, effectively allowing the guidelines to be bypassed.
items.response: The Hindu reported that the office of Delhi's Chief Electoral Officer did not respond to a request for comment.

items.headline: Civil society groups, Congress demand FIRs over bulk Form 7s seeking deletion of names
items.claim: The Hindu reported that as of September 28, 4,000 Form 7 applications seeking deletion of names had been filed in Karnataka, which it said mostly targeted Muslim voters. It reported that ten people filed Form 7s seeking deletion of 1,363 names in Babaleshwar in one day, often on forms with the voters' details already printed and only the objector's name handwritten. Civil society groups and the Karnataka Congress demanded that the Commission lodge criminal complaints.
items.response: V. Anbukumar, CEO, Karnataka, was not available for comment.

items.headline: Nearly 29,000 Form-7 applications filed during Telangana SIR
items.claim: Telangana Today reported that the Chief Electoral Officer, C. Sudharshan Reddy, said 28,753 Form 7 applications had been filed in Telangana, about 5,000 of them in Hyderabad, and that forms received in bulk would be examined with special care.
items.quote: Revealing SIR of electoral rolls status in the State on Thursday, Telangana Chief Electoral Officer C Sudharsan Reddy said 28,753 Form-7 applications were filed, so far. ... “Special care is being taken while deciding the Form-7 received in bulk. All claims and objections will be placed on the website of the CEO, so that citizens are able to see the list and lodge objections, if any,” he said.

items.headline: Telangana SIR: Congress alleges vote deletion bid in Musheerabad
items.claim: Siasat reported that the Telangana Congress complained to the Chief Electoral Officer that a BJP booth agent in Musheerabad had filed Form 7 applications against a Congress booth agent and about 30 members of his family, on forms that were printed in advance. This is the Congress's allegation.
items.quote: Kumar said that the applications were pre-printed and prepared in advance, rather than being individually and independently prepared by the concerned applicants. “The circumstances raise serious questions regarding the source from which these forms were obtained, who prepared them, who supplied the information contained in them, and whether the applications were submitted with the knowledge and consent of the persons shown as applicants.” the complaint stated.
items.response: Siasat reported that the Congress asked for an investigation to establish the facts, including a forensic examination of whether the forms came from a common source.

items.headline: Karnataka BJP Leader Withdraws Form-7 Pleas To Delete 243 Voters After SIR Row
items.claim: A BJP leader in Koppa, Chikkamagaluru, wrote on 1 October to withdraw Form 7 objections seeking the deletion of 243 voters filed on 21 and 22 September, saying the voters were found on re-verification to live within the polling stations' areas, Free Press Journal reported.
items.quote: "withdrawing the Form-7 objections submitted on September 21 and 22"
items.response: No response from the election authorities was reported.

items.headline: Karnataka SIR: ECI flags bulk Form 7 claims, orders action against false declarations
items.claim: The New Indian Express reported that the Commission wrote to election officials in Bengaluru that bulk Form 7 applications had come to its notice, with allegations that some were not authentic. It reported that the Commission directed Electoral Registration Officers to act against applicants who knowingly make false declarations, after an inquiry under Rule 20 of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960.

items.headline: After Musheerabad, Telangana Congress says it found more pre-printed Form 7s aimed at deleting Muslim voters in Bahadurpura
items.claim: The South First reported that it had seen a Form 7 from a polling station in Aliyabad, in Bahadurpura, with the voter's details printed and the objector's part left blank. The Congress alleged that such forms had been handed to BJP booth agents through the party's constituency in-charges.
items.quote: South First has seen one such pre-printed application seeking the deletion of a Muslim voter from a polling station in Aliyabad. It has the voter’s details and address pre-filled, but the applicant’s details are left blank.
items.response: The South First reported that the Chief Electoral Officer, C. Sudharshan Reddy, said at a press briefing that officials would thoroughly verify all Form 7 applications before making any decision.

items.headline: SIR: Single Jharkhand Assembly Constituency Accounts for Over a Third of Voter Deletion Requests
items.claim: Of 13,443 Form 7 applications for deletion in Jharkhand, 4,790 came from the Chatra Assembly seat, about 36% of the state's total, in figures the Chief Electoral Officer released on 1 October, The Wire reported, citing the Hindustan Times. West Singhbhum had 1,906 and Deoghar 1,099.
items.quote: About one in every three requests to remove names from Jharkhand's electoral roll has come from just one assembly constituency, data released on Thursday (October 1) by the state's chief electoral officer (CEO) revealed. ... Of the 13,443 Form 7 submitted for deletion of names, 4,790 pertain to the Chatra assembly seat in Chatra district, roughly 36% of the state's total.
items.response: The Wire reported that the Chief Electoral Officer said the Chatra figures were checked with the district administration and no bulk applications beyond the limit were found, and that address changes on Form 8 generate Form 7 entries automatically.

items.headline: Karnataka: 43.43 lakh SIR notices delivered, 84,900 Form 7 applications received so far
items.claim: Vartha Bharati reported, quoting the Chief Electoral Officer's office, that Karnataka received 8,85,952 Form 6, 4,648 Form 6A, 84,900 Form 7 and 11,78,028 Form 8 applications between 16 June and 1 October, and that 35,60,833 hearings had been held, with 7,82,304 pending.
items.response: The figures are a running count while hearings continue. Karnataka's final roll is due on 27 October 2026.

items.headline: Five FIRs filed across Karnataka over alleged misuse of Form 7, BJP threatens protest
items.claim: The News Minute reported that five FIRs were registered in Belagavi, Bidar and Mysuru over Form 7s alleged to carry false information or forged signatures, and that in Belagavi the voters' details had been filled in beforehand with the objector's name handwritten or blank.
items.quote: The names and other details of voters had already been filled in, while the names of the persons shown as objectors were either handwritten or left blank. ... None of the five FIRs filed in connection with the Karnataka cases invokes the Representation of the People Act.
items.response: The News Minute reported that Karnataka CEO V. Anbu Kumar said that although 84,900 Form 7s had been received, no one had been taken off the rolls.

items.headline: SIR: 15-Pre-Printed Form 7 Now Appear in Goshamahal Constituency
items.claim: Deccan Chronicle reported, citing Congress sources, that a BJP booth agent brought 15 pre-printed Form 7s to the booth officer at booth 173 in Goshamahal and that the booth officer refused to accept them.
items.quote: Hyderabad: After Musheerabad and Bahadurpura Assembly constituencies, 15-pre-printed Form 7, seeking deletion of Muslim names from voter lists surfaced in Goshamahal constituency. The issue came to light after the local booth level officer (BLO) refused to accept the forms allegedly submitted by BJP booth level agent (BLA).
items.response: Deccan Chronicle reported that the District Election Officer had reportedly directed the Musheerabad ERO to file criminal cases against the booth agent there.

items.headline: Owaisi says Hyderabad will see massive protests if ECI doesn’t act on Form 7 misuse
items.claim: The News Minute reported that AIMIM president Asaduddin Owaisi alleged that Form 7s were being filed to have Muslim voters deleted and warned of protests, and that Congress leaders said the pre-printed forms found in Goshamahal and Bahadurpura were unsigned and were not accepted by booth officers.
items.quote: Following the Musheerabad incident, Congress leaders said they also found pre-printed forms seeking deletion of Muslim voters in Goshamahal and Bahadurpura constituencies, but these forms were unsigned and not accepted by the Booth Level Officers (BLOs).

items.headline: Karnataka BJP leaders meet DGP, seek review of FIRs over Form 7 filings
items.claim: The News Minute reported that Karnataka BJP leaders asked the state police chief to review the FIRs against party workers, saying filing several Form 7s is not by itself a crime and the rules set no limit on their number.
items.quote: Ashoka said Congress leaders had pressured the police to register criminal cases against BJP workers. “Submitting Form 7 is not a crime. It is the Election Commission, not the police station, that has to determine the truth and validity of a voter,” he said.
items.response: The News Minute reported that Deputy Chief Minister G. Parameshwara said ministers had gone to the CEO's office to submit a memorandum.

items.headline: Contested Form 7s rejected, no bulk filings: Telangana DEO
items.claim: Siasat reported, citing PTI, that Hyderabad's District Election Officer R. V. Karnan said the Form 7s in Goshamahal and Musheerabad were not received in bulk and were rejected, the Goshamahal forms because they were unsigned and the Musheerabad ones because the electors were found living at the address.
items.quote: Greater Hyderabad Municipal Corporation (GHMC) Commissioner and District Election Officer R. V. Karnan told PTI that the Form 7 applications were not received in bulk but in much smaller numbers. In Goshamahal, the applicant did not sign the submitted forms, making them ineligible for consideration.
items.response: Siasat reported that BJP state president N. Ramchander Rao said no BJP booth agents had submitted any such Form 7 applications, and that the Chief Electoral Officer had said bulk forms from a party had to be properly enquired into and verified.

items.headline: Telangana SIR: Congress seeks SIT probe into alleged Form-7 misuse
items.claim: The News Minute quoted a memo of 5 October in which the Chief Electoral Officer, C. Sudharshan Reddy, told District Election Officers that bulk Form 7 applications had been filed and that EROs should act under Section 31 of the Representation of the People Act against anyone who knowingly made a false declaration.
items.quote: Meanwhile, the Telangana Chief Election Officer (CEO) C Sudharshan Reddy, on October 5, issued a notice stating, “[I]t has come to the notice of this office that there have been instances of filing of bulk applications in Form-7 before the EROs and it is also alleged that such forms are not genuine.”
items.response: Siasat reported that the CEO said this action would follow an inquiry. The memo itself was not found on the CEO Telangana website.

items.headline: SIR: Telangana CEO orders action over bulk Form 7 filings, Congress seeks SIT probe
items.claim: The South First reported that the Telangana Congress asked the Hyderabad Police Commissioner to register an FIR and set up a Special Investigation Team over pre-filled Form 7s in three constituencies, and to examine the BJP's role. These are the Congress's allegations.
items.quote: One such form seen by South First had the voter’s name and address pre-filled while the applicant’s details were blank. ... The Congress alleged that the forms had been printed in advance and asked the police to establish whether the persons named as applicants had actually signed them or even knew about the applications.
items.response: The South First reported that the Congress said the Police Commissioner had assured it he would study the matter and take action.

items.headline: 91,278 Form 7 applications received in Karnataka, officials says no names deleted so far
items.claim: Karnataka's Chief Electoral Officer said 91,278 Form 7 applications were received between 16 June and 4 October, that no name had yet been deleted because of one, and that each would go through a notice and hearing before an officer decided. He said EROs would inquire into bulk applications and that his office had registered no FIR, The News Minute reported.
items.quote: Karnataka has received 91,278 Form 7 applications seeking deletion of names from electoral rolls during the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR). However, no voter has been deleted through the process so far. ... “Just because objections have been filed, no name has been deleted so far from the electoral roll,” Anbukkumar said at a press conference.

items.headline: Karnataka SIR Row: FIR Against BJP BLAs For 'Fake Voter Deletion' In Jayanagar
items.claim: Jayanagar police in Bengaluru registered an FIR against two BJP booth level agents and others on a complaint by Karnataka Mahila Congress president Sowmya Reddy, The Daily Jagran reported, carrying ANI. The complaint alleged Form 7 applications with forged signatures seeking to delete 5,698 voters by falsely claiming they had shifted.
items.response: No response from the BJP, the Chief Electoral Officer or the Commission was reported.

items.headline: Goshamahal Voter Deletion Row: Owaisi Seeks ECI Action
items.claim: Deccan Chronicle reported that Asaduddin Owaisi alleged that pre-printed Form 7s seeking the deletion of 122 electors, all Muslim, were submitted at booth 28 in Goshamahal in the name of a BJP supporter, and that the booth officer refused them. This is AIMIM's allegation.
items.quote: We are placing a specific example before the Election Commission from Booth Number 28 in the Goshamahal assembly segment. As part of a deliberate plan, pre-printed Form 7 applications were submitted to delete the names of 122 electors.
items.response: Siasat reported on 5 October, citing PTI, that BJP state president N. Ramchander Rao said no BJP booth agents had submitted any such Form 7 applications.

items.headline: Police probe fake Form-7 applications seeking deletion of 31 voters in Musheerabad
items.claim: Telangana Today reported that Chikkadpally police were checking the forms, signatures and voter details in the Musheerabad case and whether similar forms were filed elsewhere, and that the forms had reportedly been rejected.
items.quote: Police officials are verifying the forms, signatures, and voter details and are also looking into who prepared and submitted the applications and whether others were involved. Officials are also checking whether similar applications were filed elsewhere. Meanwhile, the disputed applications have reportedly been rejected following scrutiny.

items.headline: 28 मतदाताओं के नाम हटाने के लिए फर्जी Form-7 का मामला, कोर्ट ने FIR के दिए आदेश
items.claim: A Judicial Magistrate First Class in Haldwani ordered the Banbhoolpura police on 6 October to register an FIR and investigate. A booth agent of a party had said that Form 7s seeking to delete 28 voters in part 134 were filed online in his name without his knowledge, and the court held that tracing who filed them needed a police investigation, Haldwani Express News reported.
items.quote: विशेष गहन पुनरीक्षण (SIR) प्रक्रिया के दौरान 28 मतदाताओं के नाम मतदाता सूची से हटाने के लिए कथित तौर पर फर्जी तरीके से Form-7 दाखिल किए जाने के मामले में न्यायिक मजिस्ट्रेट प्रथम, हल्द्वानी ने थाना बनभूलपुरा पुलिस को एफआईआर दर्ज कर विवेचना करने के निर्देश दिए हैं। ... हालांकि, अदालत ने स्पष्ट किया कि मतदाता सूची में संशोधन से संबंधित यह उपचार और कथित अपराध की पुलिस जांच दो अलग-अलग विषय हैं।
items.response: Haldwani Express News reported that the police had told the court the complaint concerned SIR Form 7s and that the complainant could object before the assistant returning officer.

items.headline: NDA leaders seek K'taka Guv intervention over 'govt interference' in SIR
items.claim: A BJP and JD(S) delegation including Union Minister H D Kumaraswamy and R Ashoka asked Governor Thaawarchand Gehlot to direct the state government to stop registering criminal cases against people who filed Form 7 objections, ThePrint reported, carrying PTI. They alleged police were being misused to intimidate BJP workers and that the Chief Electoral Office had given in to the state government.
items.quote: It urged Gehlot to issue appropriate directions to the state government to ensure that "false and unwarranted" FIRs and criminal cases under the BNS are not registered against individuals, including BJP workers, in connection with the SIR exercise.
items.response: No response from the state government, the Chief Electoral Officer or Congress was reported.

items.headline: Congress and BJP-JD(S) trade charges over bulk Form 7 filings during SIR in Karnataka
items.claim: Chief Minister D K Shivakumar alleged on 6 October that BJP and JD(S) workers had filed Form 7 applications in bulk and then collected back and destroyed more than a lakh of them, threatening booth officers, The News Minute reported. This is his allegation.
items.quote: "They have burnt them."
items.response: BJP MLC C T Ravi asked the Commission to register a case against people making baseless allegations and sought legal action against Shivakumar.

items.headline: First FIR Related to Form-7
items.claim: Deccan Chronicle reported that the Musheerabad ERO filed a police complaint, and Chikkadpally police registered a case, against a BJP booth agent who tried to submit 30 pre-printed Form 7s, the first such case in Telangana.
items.quote: The case was booked under BNS Sections 217 (giving false information to a public servant) and 318 (2) (cheating) and Section 31 of the Representation of People Act (making false declarations). ... “The BLO concerned and BLO supervisor collectively refused to receive the bulk forms in spite of repeated requests from the said BLA of BJP and have not given any acknowledgement in token of receipt…,” the FIR copy read.
items.response: Deccan Chronicle reported that the Congress welcomed the case and asked the police to find who printed and supplied the forms.

items.headline: K'taka: BJP-JDS delegation seeks withdrawal of FIR over Form-7 issue
items.claim: A BJP and JD(S) delegation led by Jayanagar MLA C K Ramamurthy went to Jayanagar police station in Bengaluru and demanded that the FIR against BJP workers over Form 7 applications be withdrawn, IANS reported. They warned of an intensified agitation if it was not, and alleged that applications meant to be confidential had been handed to Congress workers.
items.quote: The delegation demanded that the FIR be withdrawn immediately.
items.response: No police response was reported.

items.headline: K'taka: BJP-JDS delegation seeks withdrawal of FIR over Form-7 issue
items.claim: Police at Shanivarasanthe in Kodagu district registered a case against five BJP booth level workers on a complaint that they sought the deletion of 64 voters in Byadagutta village through Form 7 applications, IANS reported.
items.quote: Police have registered a case against the five persons and are investigating the allegations.

items.headline: For Every Form 6 Disposal, Six Form 7s Cleared in Delhi: Report
items.claim: The Wire reported, citing The Hindu's analysis of Delhi's constituency data, that 569 Form 6 applications and 3,209 Form 7 applications were disposed of between 31 August and 4 October, about six Form 7s for every Form 6. It said 2,352 of the Form 7s were disposed of in the last two weeks, and that 2.12 lakh Form 6 and 51,747 Form 7 applications had been submitted from 16 June, before the claims period began on 31 August.
items.quote: only 569 Form 6 applications were disposed of between August 31 and October 4
items.response: No response from the Chief Electoral Officer was reported. On 22 October the Chief Electoral Officer's office replaced the weekly disposal report on which this analysis rests, and officials said the earlier figures were wrong. The revised figures are entered separately, from The Hindu of 23 October.

items.headline: Over 24,000 Form 7 Applications Received During SIR In Telangana
items.claim: Data released by Telangana's Chief Electoral Officer on 8 October showed 24,323 Form 7 applications received from 15 June to 7 October and 12,204 names deleted, PTI reported. The figure is lower than the 28,753 Form 7s the CEO said on 1 October had been filed, and the reports do not explain the difference.
items.quote: Election authorities in Telangana on Thursday said 24,323 Form-7 applications have been received so far during SIR of electoral rolls, of which 12,204 names were removed.
items.response: State BJP president N Ramchander Rao said the Commission decides deletions only after field inquiries.

items.case: CRL.P 102783/2026 and connected matters, a BJP functionary's petition, Karnataka High Court at Dharwad
items.headline: Karnataka High Court Grants Interim Protection To BJP Leader Booked Over Alleged Attempt To Delete Muslim Voters' Names During SIR
items.claim: The Karnataka High Court at Dharwad told the police on 8 October to take no coercive steps until 13 October against a BJP functionary and two supporters booked over Form 7s against voters in Belagavi, LiveLaw and Bar and Bench reported. A Congress block agent's complaint, as the police record it, alleges they handed about 198 fabricated Form 7s to the booth officer. On 13 October Justice Venkatesh Naik T stayed the investigation until the next hearing, citing a coordinate bench's stay in similar cases on 9 October, Bar and Bench reported. The Court allowed the State to seek to have the order modified or vacated, and posted the matter for 29 October.
items.quote: Till then, the respondent-police/IO shall not take any coercive steps against the petitioners.
items.response: The Government Pleader sought time to file objections and the latest investigation report.

items.headline: Delhi CEO restricts number of Form 7 an individual can file to raise objections
items.claim: Delhi Chief Electoral Officer Ashok Kumar announced on 9 October that the Commission had decided to limit an individual voter to ten Form 7 objections for the whole claims and objections period and five a month during continuous updation, citing bulk objections on unsubstantiated grounds, IANS reported. The statement said registration officers would act against false objections under Section 31 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950.
items.quote: A maximum number of 10 Form-7 applications during the entire period of claims and objections

items.case: W.P. No. 31887 of 2026 and W.P. No. 31893 of 2026, two BJP booth agents' petitions, Karnataka High Court
items.headline: SIR: Karnataka High Court grants relief to BJP booth agents booked for attempting to delete voters
items.claim: The Karnataka High Court stayed proceedings in two FIRs against two BJP booth agents accused over bulk Form 7s against voters in Bengaluru's Malleshwaram constituency, Bar and Bench reported. The judge said the FIRs looked premature because the registration officer had not yet decided the Form 7s.
items.quote: The concerned officer will decide.
items.response: The State said the allegations of impersonation and forgery needed investigation and that the agents filed more applications than allowed. The complainant's counsel said the bulk filing was a conspiracy aimed at OBC and SC/ST voters.

items.headline: In UP SIR, ECI Software Auto-generated 87,127* Forms to Delete Voters Without a Reason
items.claim: The Reporters' Collective reported that in the Tarabganj and Pilibhit Assembly constituencies 90 per cent of Form 7 deletion requests were against Muslim voters, and that in Tarabganj 188 objections were filed under one name on the same date against voters of one booth. It said the published data give no identity of an objector beyond a name, so the objectors cannot be checked.
items.quote: Out of 4.3 lakh Form 7 applications, in two assembly constituencies in UP, people with the same name filed hundreds of requests almost exclusively against Muslim voters. In Tarabganj and Pilibhit assembly constituencies, 90 percent of the deletion requests filed were against Muslims.
items.response: The Collective said it sent questions to the Uttar Pradesh Chief Electoral Officer and the Commission and had no reply by publication. The report does not say how it determined the voters' religion.

items.headline: Tracking ECI’s U-Turns on Form 7: In West Bengal, After Allowing Unlimited Objections, ECI Caps Them at 10
items.claim: The Wire reported that on 16 January 2026, during West Bengal's extended claims period, the Commission told the state's Chief Electoral Officer in writing that the law set no limit on the number of Form 7 objections one voter could file, and that on 9 October it capped them at ten per voter for a whole claims period, in an instruction to every state. The October instruction cites a paragraph of the Manual on Electoral Rolls, 2023 against entertaining objections presented in bulk by an individual, which the January letter did not mention. Reading the Chief Electoral Officer's daily bulletins, the report counts 3,143 objections from party agents by 20 January, 2,926 from BJP agents and 217 from Trinamool agents, and finds that 2,539 of them first appear in the bulletin dated the day after the extended window closed on 19 January.
items.quote: Currently, there are no such restrictions on number of Form 7 to be filled/submitted by an elector of that constituency to ERO/AERO as per law,
items.response: The report says the Commission has not said whether objections filed in January will be looked at again.

items.headline: Nearly One-Third of Form 7 Objections in Delhi SIR Seeking Voter Deletions Not Disclosed Publicly: Report
items.claim: The Wire reported, citing The Hindu, that 4,263 of the 13,462 Form 7 applications Delhi's Chief Electoral Officer received between 31 August and 16 October, or 31.67%, had not been published in the Form 10 lists. The Manual on Electoral Rolls, 2023 requires each objection to be listed publicly for seven days before an Electoral Registration Officer can act on it.
items.quote: Essentially, if any objection has not been publicly listed, then it is invalid and cannot be acted upon. Processing such an application will be a violation of rules,
items.response: The Hindu reported that it sent questions to the Delhi Chief Electoral Officer's office and had no response by the time of publication.

items.headline: Delhi SIR: revised data show sharp increase in Form 6 disposal rate
items.claim: Delhi's Chief Electoral Officer replaced the weekly report of applications disposed of on 22 October, and officials told The Hindu that the figures published until then were wrong. The revised report shows 1,07,451 of 4,59,796 Form 6 applications for inclusion and 47,105 of 67,709 Form 7 applications disposed of from 31 August to 18 October, about 23% and 70%. The earlier report had shown 1,238 Form 6 disposals to 11 October. Tri Nagar is the only constituency with no Form 6 disposal recorded in any of the seven weeks.
items.quote: The weekly data being uploaded till now was wrong and it was not reflecting the disposals that happened since August 31, we noticed after the newspaper report,
items.response: The Hindu attributes the quoted explanation to an unnamed official and does not say which office the official works in. More than 3.5 lakh Form 6 applications were still to be disposed of. Claims close on 30 October, every application is to be disposed of by 30 November, and the final roll is due on 4 December.

items.headline: Karnataka SIR: Form 7 submissions surged from 58,475 to 2.28 lakh in 1 month, shows data
items.claim: Karnataka received 2,28,917 Form 7 applications between 16 June and 22 October, 1,70,442 of them after 23 September, when the count stood at 58,475, The Indian Express reported from official data. The Chief Electoral Officer's office said every Form 7 received up to 23 September had been cleared on priority and that hearings for all 43.82 lakh voters sent notices were over. Bangalore Urban had the most submissions in the paper's table, 24,268. The ruling Congress has alleged that the BJP is misusing Form 7 to file objections in bulk.
items.quote: All Form-7 applications received up to September 23 have been cleared on priority, the Karnataka Chief Electoral Officer office said in a statement issued on Friday.
items.response: After a Congress protest at the Chief Electoral Officer's office earlier this month, the Chief Electoral Officer directed Electoral Registration Officers to look into the allegations. The state BJP has rejected them. The final roll is due on 27 October.

items.headline: Uttarakhand ERO refused BJP worker’s bulk Form 7 objections. After ECI complaint, 5,359 were accepted
items.claim: Newslaundry found 4,390 names on Kichha's draft roll that are missing from the final roll published on 3 October. About 670 of them had Form 7 objections filed against them in August, 509 by a single BJP booth level agent, and the other 3,720 had no objection against them and were deleted on the ground of logical discrepancies. Of the 6,884 Form 7 objections accepted in Kichha, 5,359 were that agent's, and he filed more Form 7 objections than anyone else in Uttarakhand. He told Newslaundry that the Electoral Registration Officer at first refused his bulk objections and took them after he complained to the Election Commission by email, and Newslaundry could not verify what the email said. Form 10 data from the Chief Electoral Officer's office show 504 of his accepted objections with an acceptance date of 14 August, a day after claims and objections closed. Newslaundry reported that every name in his objections was Muslim. He said the party had received information that about 6,000 electors enrolled in Kichha were also enrolled in five nearby constituencies of Uttar Pradesh.
items.quote: Of the 4,390 names missing from Kichha’s final electoral roll, 3,720 had no objections filed against them. The ERO deleted these voters on the basis of logical discrepancies, a mismatch in voter data that the ECI believes requires additional verification before the electoral roll is finalised.
items.response: The Kichha Electoral Registration Officer, Gaurav Pandey, neither confirmed nor denied the agent's account, would not say whether the Commission had directed him, and said the deletions followed the Commission's rules. Newslaundry said the Commission acknowledged its questions and did not answer them, and that it had asked the Chief Electoral Officer why objections were accepted after the deadline. The Congress MLA for Kichha, Tilak Raj Behar, said the objections rested on false information. The report does not say how it established the electors' religion.

items.headline: Dharavi man booked for filing 24 voter roll objections in a single day, exceeding ECI limit
items.claim: The Dharavi police registered a case under Section 31 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950 against a resident who had submitted 24 Form 7 applications in one day in the 178-Dharavi constituency, above the Election Commission's limit of ten a day, the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation said on 24 October, The Hindu reported. The corporation alleged that the applications carried false and incorrect information. Mumbai's draft rolls were published on 31 August and claims and objections ran to 26 October.
items.quote: Under the ECI’s guidelines, an individual can submit a maximum of 10 Form 7 applications per day.
items.response: The report gives no account from the accused. Section 31 covers anyone who knowingly makes a false statement or declaration in connection with the roll.

items.headline: Over 61,000 Form-7 applications filed by election officials in Karnataka, none cites reason
items.claim: At least 61,059 Form 7 applications seeking deletions from Karnataka's rolls were filed by Electoral Registration Officers and Assistant Electoral Registration Officers themselves, and none gives a reason for the deletion, which the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960 require, The Hindu reported. Officers listed as the objectors said the system generated the forms with their digital signatures when electors sent notices for no mapping or logical discrepancies could not be reached at hearings and were marked ineligible. Only 192 such applications were filed between 24 August and 23 September, and more than 60,800 between 24 September and 22 October, including 10,105 on 22 October, the last day for disposal. The paper's chart puts more than 53,000 of the officers' applications in the week from 16 to 22 October, with the most on one day, 11,760, on 19 October. In every case the paper checked on the Commission's portal the elector had already been deleted, including electors against whom the application came after 23 September. In the Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike South district officers filed 10,374 of 17,491 applications, and in at least 26 constituencies officers filed more than voters or third parties did.
items.quote: Electoral Registration Officers (EROs) and Assistant Electoral Registration Officers (AEROs), listed as the objectors in these applications, said the system “auto-generated” the forms with their digital signatures when voters could not be reached during hearings on notices issued for no mapping or logical discrepancies, and the voters were therefore marked as “ineligible”.
items.response: The officers said they had been told to file Form 7 for electors who had shifted, had a duplicate entry, were underage, had died or were not citizens. The report gives no reply from the Chief Electoral Officer. Rule 17 of the 1960 Rules says a claim or objection not lodged within the period or in the prescribed form and manner shall be rejected by the registration officer. The paper also found 13,808 fewer Form 7 applications for 24 September to 22 October in the Commission's Form 10 records than the Chief Electoral Officer's statements give.

items.headline: ECI to soon launch a single-point App for stakeholders; to subsume over existing 40 IT Apps with enhanced UI/UX
items.claim: The Commission announced in May 2025 that it was building ECINET, one platform to bring together more than 40 of its apps and websites for voters, election officials and other users.
items.quote: The new one-stop platform, ECINET, will integrate and reorient over 40 of ECI’s existing mobile and web applications. ... To ensure that data is as accurate as possible, the data on ECINET will be entered solely by the authorized ECI official.

items.headline: Order of 19.01.2026, W.P.(C) 1089/2025
items.claim: The Supreme Court recorded, from the documents before it, what the logical discrepancy category in West Bengal covered and that about 1.36 crore voters fell in it.
items.quote: The documents brought on record by the parties indicate that, within the category of logical discrepancies include, inter alia, a mismatch of the father’s name, a mismatch of parents’ ages, a difference in parents’ ages of more than 50 years, a difference in grandparents’ ages of less than 40 years, and those having more than six progeny.

items.headline: ECINET Digital Platform launched at IICDEM-2026
items.claim: The Commission launched ECINET formally on 22 January 2026 and said its trial version had already been used during the Bihar election and the SIR.
items.quote: The beta version was successfully piloted during the 2025 Bihar Assembly Elections and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), enabling the Election Commission to deliver enhanced citizen-centric electoral services and make available all election-related information at the click of a button.

items.headline: Press note No.EL.63/2026/50: CEO Meghalaya Reviews Notice and Hearing Phase of SIR 2026
items.claim: Meghalaya's Chief Electoral Officer listed six checks that ECINET used to flag mapping discrepancies in the third phase, among them a sibling age gap under nine months.
items.quote: The discrepancies identified through ECINET are: mismatch between the elector's name and the name available in the SIR 2005 records; mismatch between the elector's parent's name and the corresponding name recorded in SIR 2005; age difference between the elector and parent being less than 15 years or more than 50 years; age gap of less than nine months between siblings linked to the same parent; more than six children being linked to the same parent; and age difference of less than 40 years between an elector and grandparent.

items.headline: The meeting of the Commission was held today i.e. 26.09.2026 at 3:00 PM
items.claim: After its full meeting on 26 September 2026 the Commission said field officers have access to ECINET by role, set up a committee with an independent expert to check ECINET against the law, and said new IT modules would first go to a committee of officers.
items.quote: Field officers have role-based access to the ECINET system as per their statutory powers. A Committee headed by Sr. Deputy Election Commissioner (DEC) and including an independent expert from IIT/IIIT will review the ECINET to double-check that it complies with the provisions of the Acts and Rules and submit report to the Commission. ... Henceforth, all the new initiatives about IT modules and portals will be discussed in the Committee of Officers (COO) before approval by the Commission.

items.headline: MP Special Intensive Revision: 100 Forms A Day, BLOs Complain Of Impossible Targets; Voters Can’t Find Old Records
items.claim: Booth officers in Bhopal told the Free Press Journal they were asked to upload 100 forms a day and could not, because the booth officers' app server was down or very slow.
items.quote: They are being asked to collect and upload 100 forms a day. It is an impossible target to achieve, they say, adding that they are unable to feed the data of voters as the server of BLO App is either down or very slow.

items.headline: How ECI’s dubious software branded 3.66 crore voters in West Bengal and Madhya Pradesh as suspects
items.claim: The Reporters' Collective reported, from internal Commission records it acquired, that the Commission's software initially flagged 1.31 crore voters in West Bengal and 2.35 crore in Madhya Pradesh for logical discrepancies, and that officials had no written instructions on how to resolve them. It reported that no criteria for deciding which flagged voters to summon had been made public.
items.response: The Collective said the Commission did not answer its question on how flagged voters were chosen, and that questions sent to the Commission and three state offices on testing and procedure went unanswered.

items.headline: Verified: ECI’s top West Bengal officer sent orders to state officials for SIR on WhatsApp
items.claim: The Reporters' Collective reported that on 29 December 2025 the West Bengal Chief Electoral Officer's office told state officials in writing that the logical discrepancy software was faulty because the 2002 roll had not been digitised accurately.
items.quote: On December 29, after the enumeration phase was complete, the CEO West Bengal’s office admitted on record to state officials that the software finding ‘logical discrepancies’ was malfunctioning. This was because the base data, the 2002 voter list, had not been digitised accurately, the CEO admitted.
items.response: The Collective said the Commission and the West Bengal Chief Electoral Officer did not reply to its questions on the WhatsApp instructions.

items.outlet: Siasat (IANS, citing officials of the Chief Electoral Officer, West Bengal)
items.headline: West Bengal SIR: ECI explains why ‘logical discrepancy’ cases are high
items.claim: Officials of West Bengal's Chief Electoral Officer told IANS that the logical discrepancy check caught people who had falsely linked themselves to unrelated voters, and gave examples they said were found at hearings.
items.quote: “There have been cases where eight to ten voters were shown as sons or daughters of a single senior citizen voter during progeny mapping. However, during hearings, it was found that the senior citizen had only two children and had no blood relationship with most of those listed as his sons or daughters,” said an official from the CEO’s office.

items.headline: BLO App underwent 30 changes in two months in Tamil Nadu
items.claim: The New Indian Express reported that the Android version of the booth officers' app was updated 31 times between 13 November 2025 and 20 January 2026, with no user manual for the updates, and that officials relied on the app to learn what the revision allowed.
items.quote: TNIE’s analysis of iOS and Android version logs showed that the Android version underwent 31 updates between November 13 (version 8.65) and January 20 (9.10), which is at an average of a new version released every second day. ... “The options available on the BLO App informed us what is permitted and what is not rather than detailed instructions or training material regarding the process or the use of the app,” a district-level official said.

items.headline: BLO App underwent 30 changes in two months in Tamil Nadu
items.claim: The same report quoted a Chennai booth officer who said the app often froze on her phone, so that data was lost or finished work had to be done again.
items.quote: A BLO from Chennai told TNIE that her phone couldn’t handle the application and frequently froze, leading to loss of data or redoing of completed work.

items.headline: ECI misled the Supreme Court on SIR in West Bengal
items.claim: The Reporters' Collective reported that hearing notices in West Bengal were generated in bulk by the Commission's software for logical discrepancies, and that two EROs it spoke to, with a few deputies, were signing 4,000 to 5,000 printed notices each day. It reported that the software transliterated names from Bengali into English before matching, so that spellings such as Xalxo and Khalkho triggered a discrepancy. The Collective said this showed the Commission had misled the Supreme Court, where it said there was no automated generation of notices.
items.response: The Collective said the Commission had not responded by publication. It set its finding against the Commission's submission to the Court that "There is no automated generation of notices" and that officers were "signing them off after application of mind".

items.headline: How ECI Tailored the Voter Registration in West Bengal “As it Deemed Fit”
items.claim: The Reporters' Collective reported that in West Bengal the logical discrepancy check flagged five kinds of mismatch, from spelling differences between the Bengali 2002 roll and the English draft to age gaps with parents and grandparents.
items.quote: The discrepancies were of five kinds, as per ECI’s new algorithm: Differences in spelling between the names in the 2002 in Bengali script and in the 2025 draft voter rolls in English More than six voters had linked themselves to a single ancestor from the 2003 list; The age gap between a voter and their parent fell outside the 15-to-45-year range; A cited grandparent was less than 40 years older than the voter; The gender of the voter did not align with the name provided.
items.response: The Collective said it sent detailed questions to the Commission and had no answer by publication.

items.headline: How ECI Tailored the Voter Registration in West Bengal “As it Deemed Fit”
items.claim: The Reporters' Collective reported that a registration officer showed its reporter that the button to clear voters with a name mismatch had disappeared from ERONET since that morning, so such cases now needed the district officer's approval.
items.quote: “These options keep changing every other day,” the ERO told me. “Till this morning, for logical discrepancies with name mismatch, ERONET was allowing me to verify the elector by myself. Now, when I open ERONET, that button has disappeared. Now, these have to be approved by the DEO.”
items.response: The Collective said it sent detailed questions to the Commission and had no answer by publication.

items.headline: Express Special | EC changes Form 6 for new voters without amendment to rules; seeks SIR details of parents
items.claim: The Indian Express reported that the online Form 6 on the Commission's ECINET portal carried a new declaration asking whether the applicant or their parents or grandparents were in the electoral roll of the last SIR, although the statutory form had not been amended. It reported that although the section was not marked mandatory, applicants could not submit the form without completing it, and that the downloadable Form 6 on the same portal did not include it.
items.response: The EC did not respond to a request for comment and Legislative Department Secretary Rajiv Mani could not be reached despite repeated attempts.

items.headline: SIR: Not even 0.5% submit enumeration forms online amid website glitches
items.claim: The Hindu reported that 13 days into the Karnataka SIR only 0.41% of enumeration forms had been submitted online, and that voters complained of captcha failures, server errors and an ECINet search that failed to find records appearing in the published rolls. It reported that online submission required a current mobile number linked to the voter's EPIC.
items.response: Karnataka Chief Electoral Officer V. Anbu Kumar said the process was still under way. However, the CEO did not comment on the technical glitches reported by voters.

items.headline: SIR: ECINET Portal Faces Peak-Hour Glitches
items.claim: Deccan Chronicle reported that people filling in enumeration forms on ECINET in Telangana kept being sent back to the home page, and an official put it down to the load from voters in more than a dozen states at once.
items.quote: Officials admitted the portal was hit by server overload as voters from over a dozen states under Phase 3 of SIR accessed it simultaneously. “It is a fact that people are facing issues. In Telangana, there is no need to panic as the ECI has extended the deadline till August 3,” a senior official told Deccan Chronicle.

items.headline: ‘Illegal, unauthorised’: Election Commissioners objected to Form 6 change
items.claim: The Indian Express reported, from internal records it investigated, that on May 16 Election Commissioner Vivek Joshi recorded that Form 6 is prescribed by statute and cannot be altered without amending the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, and that Commissioner Sukhbir Singh Sandhu concurred on May 19. It reported that the declaration was added to the online form anyway, and that on August 13 Sandhu wrote that the changes were unauthorised and illegal and must be removed immediately.

items.headline: Election Commissioners knocked on Cabinet Secretary’s door over voter software integrity
items.claim: The Indian Express reported that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi warned on file, from November 2025 to August 2026, that control of the electoral roll software was being centralised in the Commission's IT division. It reported that on August 14 Sandhu wrote that many Chief Electoral Officers, District Election Officers and Electoral Registration Officers had told him they lacked proper and complete access to ERONet, and that on July 29 both Commissioners wrote separately to the Cabinet Secretary about a change in work allocation.
items.response: The Election Commission and the two ECs, Sandhu and Joshi, did not respond to calls and questionnaires emailed by The Indian Express seeking comment.

items.headline: The many categories of SIR’s logical discrepancy list keep voters on toes
items.claim: The Hindu reported that up to 11 categories of logical discrepancy were being applied in the third phase of the SIR, up from four when the concept was introduced in West Bengal. They include a sibling age gap of nine months or less, which flagged a Delhi resident's twin children, and a marital mapping mismatch where a woman is linked to her father in the old roll and her husband in the new. It reported that the term has never been clearly defined in any official communication.

items.headline: 8 emails in 7 days, but valid Goa voters still left out: EC’s flawed system
items.claim: The Indian Express reported that Goa's Electoral Registration Officers heard electors flagged for logical discrepancies and found 97 of them eligible, but could not reverse the earlier decisions on ECINET because the permission was controlled from Delhi. It reported that the Goa Chief Electoral Officer's office wrote eight times in seven days asking for a rollback option, and that all 97 were missing from the final roll published on February 21 and were still missing on September 20.
items.response: Goa's Chief Electoral Officer, Sanjay Goel, told the paper the decision not to include them was the Commission's. The Indian Express later reported that the Commission said, after its meeting of 26 September, that 81 of the 97 had filled Form 6 and that the Chief Electoral Officer had been told to help include them.

items.headline: ECINet is decentralised, only designated officials have access, says ECI
items.claim: Commission officials said ECINET is decentralised, that each field officer acts through their own login, and that nobody at headquarters can perform those officers' statutory functions. ERONET is now part of ECINET.
items.quote: “No one else can perform their statutory function on ECINet, including any other officer of the ECI,” an official said. Cybersecurity for the platform is, however, provided centrally by the ECI. ... Official documents refer to it as the “Electoral Roll module of ECINET Portal (previously ERONET)”.

items.headline: Delhi SIR: Over 350 names already marked ineligible; CEO warns against deletion on flimsy grounds
items.claim: The Hindu reported that more than 350 Delhi electors had been marked ineligible within a month of hearings, about 200 of them in Vikaspuri, and officials said the marking could not be rolled back by the registration officer or the state's Chief Electoral Officer.
items.quote: Of the 350 electors already marked ineligible less than a month into the hearings process, about 200 are from the Vikaspuri constituency; once a voter is marked ineligible, this cannot be rolled back at the level of ERO or State CEO, officials said
items.response: The Delhi Chief Electoral Officer wrote to officers on 25 September 2026 setting a 10-point checklist before marking anyone ineligible and telling them not to delete names on flimsy or frivolous grounds.

items.headline: Maharashtra Poll Chief Seeks More ERO Powers As ECINet Faces Scrutiny Over SIR
items.claim: Outlook, citing NDTV, reported that Maharashtra's Chief Electoral Officer S Chockalingam asked for four changes to the ECINET software and more discretion for registration officers in logical discrepancy cases.
items.quote: Chockalingam has also sought four changes in the ECINet software, including for cases marked as “logical discrepancies”.
items.response: The Commission said on 26 September that several portal upgrades had already been made on inputs from state Chief Electoral Officers and that further flexibility needed by field officers would be made operational.

items.headline: EC removes Form 6 change two Commissioners had called ‘illegal’
items.claim: The Indian Express reported that on the night of 29 to 30 September 2026 the Commission removed the SIR declaration from the online Form 6 on ECINET for states where the final SIR rolls have been published. It reported that the declaration remained for states where the SIR is still ongoing.
items.response: The article cites the Commission's September 26 announcement that ‘for non-SIR period, the Forms applicable as per Rules (the Registration of Electors Rules 1960) will be used’.

items.headline: Cong accuses EC of 'lying' about ECINet, calls for accountability
items.claim: Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh alleged that by restricting registration officers' access to the ECINet roll system and overruling them in Goa, West Bengal and other states, the Commission broke the Representation of the People Act, 1950.
items.quote: “By restricting access of Electoral Registration Officers (EROs) to the ECINet voter roll system and by overruling EROs in states like Goa, West Bengal and others, the ECI controlled by the CEC has violated The Representation of the People Act, 1950 and the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960,” Ramesh said.
items.response: PTI recalled that the Commission, under fire over objections from two of its Commissioners, had said differing views are a normal part of deliberation and that all its orders carry full legal sanction and follow established statutory procedures.

items.headline: After 13 crore names dropped from draft rolls, EC orders ‘left out’ voter drive
items.claim: The Indian Express reported a letter of 29 September from the Commission’s Secretary ordering a special drive to enrol "left out and young/first time eligible electors" in the 20 states and union territories where the revision is complete, using the statutory Form 6, with the added declaration kept for the revision phase only. It reported that at a video conference with all Chief Electoral Officers, the states were told to compare the roll from before the revision with the one after, list those left off or deleted, visit them at home and help those left out fill in Form 6, with help from the parties’ booth agents.
items.response: The letter of 29 September itself was not found. The Commission's letter of 1 October, which continues it, is in the timeline above. The Commission’s press note of 26 September, in the timeline above, had already ordered the drive, and Uttarakhand’s Chief Electoral Officer set out its steps in a press note of 3 October.

items.headline: EC explains new ERONET options for SIR notice disposal to EROs through demo video; no written instructions yet
items.claim: The Hindu reported that the options reached Delhi officers on 30 September and only the ten states and union territories where the third phase was still under way, and that a case marked ineligible still could not be reversed.
items.quote: EROs in Delhi could access the options from September 30, while the eight-minute video explaining the changes was shown to them at a meeting on Saturday (October 3, 2026). ... While the new options let EROs clear notice cases faster, including those where documents are unavailable, based on their satisfaction, they still cannot reverse a case once an elector has been marked ineligible, officials said.
items.response: The Delhi CEO’s office and the EC did not respond to queries on why the options were introduced at this stage.

items.headline: 'Misleading': ECI fact-checks Rahul Gandhi's Form 6 claim, cites SC ruling on Bihar SIR order
items.claim: Rahul Gandhi of the Congress, the Leader of the Opposition, said the Chief Election Commissioner had changed Form 6 illegally and unilaterally. The Commission replied on X that the statement was misleading, that its Bihar order of 24 June 2025 had the Commission's unanimous approval and was upheld by the Supreme Court on 27 May 2026, and that its press note of 26 September said the declaration attached to Form 6 had been upheld, Business Today reported.
items.quote: "It is now established beyond doubt that Gyanesh Kumar changed Form 6 illegally and unilaterally," Gandhi said. ... Fact Check ❌The statement made in this post is misleading ✅1) The order for SIR in Bihar issued on 24 June 2025 was issued with the unanimous approval of the Commission. This order has been upheld by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in its judgment dated 27 May 2026 ✅2) In its Press Note No. 120 dated 26 September 2026, in Point 1(iii), ECI has stated that, "The declaration attached to Form 6 for SIR has been upheld by the Hon'ble Supreme Court." #ECIFactCheck

items.headline: Dozen Bengal tribunal judges flag EC portal: ‘Can’t restore deleted voters’
items.claim: The Indian Express reported that at a meeting on 11 August 2026 more than a dozen West Bengal appeal tribunal judges recorded that the Commission's portal did not let them serve notices, hold virtual hearings, restore a deleted voter or give appellants a copy of the order.
items.quote: “There is no mechanism to hold virtual hearings in case the Tribunal intends to hear the parties…Once the appeal is disposed of either by way of deletion or inclusion of the voter, it cannot be restored on the portal if the restoration is needed on account of direction of the judicial order or otherwise.”
items.response: The paper said it emailed the Commission and the Registrar General of the Calcutta High Court on 1 October and received no response.

items.headline: ECINET flaws were flagged to poll body, cyber-security agency CERT-In in July: Researcher
items.claim: Hindustan Times reported that a security researcher emailed CERT-In on 8 July 2026, copied to the Commission's complaints address, about flaws in the voter-services website and the ECINET app. The worst, in the researcher's account, let anyone obtain election officials' names and mobile numbers without logging in.
items.quote: The issue [the researcher] rated as critical concerns a server behind the voter portal. He says it returned the names and mobile numbers of election officials to requests that carried no login, CAPTCHA or visible limit on the number of requests.
items.response: HT said neither CERT-In nor the Commission answered its questions of 5 October. On 6 October CERT-In told the researcher that one flaw, the hardcoded encryption key he rated least serious, had been fixed and that work on the rest was under progress. HT said none of the flaws related directly to registration officers' access to the roll, and that the email alleged no theft or misuse of data.

items.headline: ECINET designed to centralise voter deletions from BJP headquarters, Congress alleges
items.claim: Congress alleged after the Hindustan Times report that ECINET was designed to centralise deletions and additions from the BJP's headquarters. This is a party's allegation. Hindustan Times had said none of the flaws it reported related directly to registration officers' access to the roll.
items.quote: The Congress on Thursday alleged that the Election Commission’s online portal for voter registration and related services was designed to “centralise all deletions and additions from the Bharatiya Janata Party headquarters”.
items.response: Scroll did not report a response from the Commission to this allegation.

items.headline: 'Was Ghosted': Why [the researcher] Wrote to Election Commission and CERT-in in July
items.claim: The security researcher who reported the ECINET flaws told The Wire that CERT-In and the Commission did not reply to him until a Hindustan Times reporter contacted them. CERT-In then said one issue had been resolved, which he said was the most minor. He said the flaws affected at least eight parts of the Commission's systems, including the Suvidha portal and ECORE.
items.quote: According to him, it was the most minor of the lot.
items.response: No statement from the Commission was reported.

items.headline: In UP SIR, ECI Software Auto-generated 85,854 Forms to Delete Voters Without a Reason
items.claim: The Reporters' Collective reported, from more than 4.3 lakh Form 7 disclosures on the Uttar Pradesh Chief Electoral Officer's website, that 87,127 deletion requests were filed by registration officers between 15 March and 2 April 2026 and that 85,854 of them gave no reason. Registration officers it spoke to said ERONET generated a Form 7 carrying their digital signature whenever they did not approve a voter at a hearing. It also reported that 1,10,476 deletion requests from individuals were accepted after the deadline.
items.quote: Our analysis of the data scraped from the ECI’s website shows that 85,854 (98.5 percent) of the 87,127 requests filed by EROs and AEROs have no reason mentioned for deletion.
items.response: The Collective said the Chief Electoral Officer and the Commission had not replied by publication. On 13 October 2026 IANS reported the Chief Electoral Officer's office calling the claims misleading and saying "Notices, hearings, scrutiny and recorded orders preceded action. Pending cases were decided after 6 March as per procedure."

items.headline: The ECI Software Deleted 5.38 Lakh Bengal Voters With Auto-Generated Rejections Without Citing a Reason
items.claim: The Wire reported that 5,38,320 names were deleted from West Bengal's roll between the draft of December 2025 and the final roll of 28 February 2026 through Form 7s that the Commission's software generated in the officer's name when an officer did not approve an elector at a hearing, and that 7,733 more were deleted on Form 7s that people had filed. In the Form 10 registers it read for 284 of the 294 constituencies, 5,23,998 of 5,24,420 Form 7 deletions give the Electoral Registration Officer as the objector and leave the reason blank, and 422 give an individual objector. The Chief Electoral Officer's statement of 6 March 2026 said the state's Form 7 figure included these auto-generated forms, and that the Commission had sent the figure of 5,38,320 by email on 28 February.
items.quote: The figure of deletion due to Form 7 as mentioned, includes the auto generated Form 7 generated due to rejection of Enumeration Forms (EFs) as electors not found eligible for Final Roll. This Figure which was received from ECI (Election Commission of India) by mail on 28.02.26 in 5,38,320 (sic).
items.response: The Wire reported that the Additional Chief Electoral Officer of West Bengal told it Form 10 gives no option to record details, and that those deleted can apply again through Form 6.

items.headline: Audit finds Bengal-specific access curbs in ECINET code
items.claim: The Hindustan Times reported a review of ECINET's publicly served code by Saurav Rajput, a data scientist at the civic-tech initiative Charchagram, which found an exception written into the code that can bar Electoral Registration Officers and Assistant Electoral Registration Officers in West Bengal from the View Enumeration Form Details tile on the SIR Phase II landing page and from the notice-and-hearing dashboard. The review found no such exclusion for these officers in any other state. The enumeration form page lists each form with its documents and the booth level officer's recommendation, and holds documents labelled as hearing orders. The review read only the code a browser receives before login, on 2, 6, 7 and 9 October and in code fetched on 19 October, so it cannot say whether the rule was ever used, whether the server enforces it, or when it was added. The paper could not verify the review independently.
items.quote: West Bengal is separately hard-coded in the codebase and excluded from it (for ERO and AERO).
items.response: The Hindustan Times reported that the Election Commission did not answer a questionnaire it sent.

items.headline: On ECINet platform, access for States can be switched off and on centrally: report
items.claim: The Hindu reported another finding from Saurav Rajput's review of ECINET's code for the civic-tech initiative Charchagram. Behind the official login the portal has an area for managing State Nodal Officers, and each officer's row has a disable button whose confirmation says the user will no longer be able to access the application. Separately, the code carries the message that viewing enumeration form details is not enabled for the selected State, which the review reads as a feature switched on or off State by State. The review read only code the site serves before login. The paper says it was not clear since when the feature has been on the portal, which was launched in January 2026, and the reviewer said he had seen it since 28 September.
items.quote: On disabling this State Nodal Officer, the user will no longer be able to access the application.
items.response: The Hindu carried a statement by the Congress general secretary (communications), Jairam Ramesh, that the ECINET system and the Commission's IT division had overruled the statutory authority of Electoral Registration Officers. It reported no response from the Commission.

items.headline: TMC seeks EC explanation on Bengal specific feature in voter’s enumeration forms in ECINET
items.claim: Millennium Post reported that the Trinamool Congress, reacting to the Hindustan Times report of the same day on the West Bengal rule in ECINET's code, asked the Election Commission who had authorised the Bengal-specific changes, why West Bengal was treated differently from other states, who is accountable and what safeguards protect every eligible voter's rights. The party also asked when the Chief Election Commissioner would take responsibility and resign.
items.quote: Who authorised these Bengal-specific changes, and Why?
items.response: The report carries no response from the Commission.

items.headline: ECINET Audit Finds State-Level Access Could be Restricted by Election Commission, VIP Tags for Voters
items.claim: The Wire reported three findings from Saurav Rajput's review of ECINET's code for the civic-tech initiative Charchagram, made on 2, 6, 7 and 9 October from code the site serves publicly, with no passwords and no use of ECINET's programming interfaces. Besides the State Nodal Officer controls and the West Bengal rule in the two reports before it, the review found code showing that the officials' portal marks some voters with a gold VIP symbol on the screen that shows the documents in an enumeration form, and a button that downloads a list of these VIP electors by Assembly constituency, which can be narrowed by state, district, constituency and polling part. The criteria for marking a voter are not known. The review cannot say whether any of these features were used, by whom or how often. The Reporters' Collective earlier reported a Mark VIP module in the booth level officers' app, and Charchagram says its review examined the other end of that chain.
items.quote: At present, we cannot say whether these features have been used, or prove how they have been used
items.response: The report carries no response from the Commission.

items.headline: Details of software used in SIR exempt from RTI, Election Commission cites 'trade secrets'
items.claim: In a reply dated 16 October to an RTI application from a social activist in Karimnagar, the Commission declined to give the name and version of the software it used to find errors and anomalies in the rolls during the revision, citing commercial confidence, trade secrets and intellectual property under Section 8(1)(d), the Hindustan Times reported. It called the questions on automatic flagging, artificial intelligence and safeguards against wrongful flagging a clarification outside the definition of information, and cited Section 8(1)(g) on who reviews flagged records.
items.quote: no new software has been developed or procured for the SIR exercise
