items.response: The Commission said Electoral Registration Officers decide on including or excluding an elector on the basis of facts and records, and that under Sections 13B(1) and 13B(2) of the Representation of the People Act, 1950 the officer of each constituency prepares and revises its roll.

sections.title: Instructions given without a written order

items.headline: Verified: ECI’s top West Bengal officer sent orders to state officials for SIR on WhatsApp
items.claim: The Reporters' Collective reported that West Bengal's Chief Electoral Officer sent instructions on a WhatsApp group of district magistrates that brought forward the enumeration deadline and asked officers to mark voters absent before the written deadline. The Trinamool Congress had first made the allegation before the Supreme Court.
items.quote: However, instructions issued solely on WhatsApp, advanced this date and asked officials to mark voters absent even before this deadline elapsed. ... We verified the informal instructions. Two officials showed the messages
items.response: The Collective said the Commission and the West Bengal Chief Electoral Officer did not reply to its questions on the WhatsApp instructions.

items.headline: How ECI Tailored the Voter Registration in West Bengal “As it Deemed Fit”
items.claim: The Reporters' Collective reported that district magistrates of at least three West Bengal districts wrote to the state election office asking for a written procedure for logical discrepancy cases, and that the portal accepted only the 12 listed documents.
items.quote: “Regarding logical discrepancies for mapped cases: An SOP may kindly be provided of logical discrepancy cases…and the role of BLO, ERO/AERO and DEO. Also, instruction may be provided about requisite documents to be taken at the time of hearing by ERO/AERO for such cases. It may be kindly noted that there is no provision for uploading other than 12 categories at the portal at the moment,” said the letter to the CEO.
items.response: The Collective reported that the officers received no response and carried on with their own methods.

items.headline: How ECI Tailored the Voter Registration in West Bengal “As it Deemed Fit”
items.claim: A registration officer told The Reporters' Collective that officers were told orally to ask unmapped electors for a second document besides Aadhaar, and that the software for a time would not accept Aadhaar alone. The Collective said it could not check this claim.
items.quote: “While this contradicts the original SIR instructions, we received no written orders. Just the software stopped allowing us (EROs) to only upload Aadhar. We were required by design to upload additional documents. The feature seemed to have disappeared now,” he said while showing us the interface. The Collective could not independently verify this claim.

items.headline: SIR: EC state poll machinery to share details of 'suspected foreigners' with authorities
items.claim: PTI reported that the Commission's written instructions of 14 May 2026 for the third phase told registration officers to refer suspected foreign nationals to the authority under the Citizenship Act.
items.quote: In a detailed set of instructions circulated on May 14 to state chief electoral officers on procedure to be followed while holding SIR, the poll authority said "... Also, electoral registration officers (EROs) will refer cases of suspected foreign nationals to the competent authority under the Citizenship Act, 1955. For these purposes, assistant EROs shall exercise ERO's powers independently..."

items.headline: EC explains new ERONET options for SIR notice disposal to EROs through demo video; no written instructions yet
items.claim: A Delhi registration officer told The Hindu that officers were first told to identify suspected foreigners during enumeration and later told in the middle of it to stop, and that many oral instructions had been taken back.
items.quote: “Since SIR was announced, we have received a lot of instructions, some written and some oral. Many have since been taken back. For instance, we were told to identify ‘suspected foreigners’ along with Absent, Shifted, Dead and Duplicate, and then, in the middle of the enumeration phase in Delhi, we were told not to identify or report such cases.”
items.response: The Delhi CEO's office and the EC did not respond to The Hindu's queries on why the new ERONET options were introduced at that stage.

items.headline: EC explains new ERONET options for SIR notice disposal to EROs through demo video; no written instructions yet
items.claim: The Hindu reported that new ERONET options letting registration officers clear notice cases without a hearing or documents were explained only through an eight-minute video from the Commission's IT department, with no written instruction.
items.quote: Days after adding new options to its ERONET portal that allow Electoral Registration Officers (EROs) to dispose of notice cases without hearings or documents, the Election Commission (EC) is now explaining the changes to officials through a demonstration video prepared by the Election Commission’s Information Technology (IT) Department, with no written documents circulated so far, sources told The Hindu.
items.response: The Delhi CEO’s office and the EC did not respond to queries on why the options were introduced at this stage.

items.headline: Maharashtra CEO Seeks Changes to Form 6
items.claim: Maharashtra's Chief Electoral Officer wrote to the Commission asking it to change Form 6 so that electors left off the draft in the revision can register again without declaring themselves first-time voters, Deccan Chronicle reported. The letter says officers find it hard to persuade such electors to sign a form that carries a penalty for a false declaration. It asks for the words "new voters" to be taken out of the form's title, for a separate declaration for people who were enrolled before and are no longer on any roll, and for a place to give the earlier EPIC number.
items.quote: Election officials have reported difficulties in persuading such voters to submit Form 6, as many fear that declaring themselves first-time applicants despite having been registered previously could expose them to legal action.
items.response: Officials said that any change to the statutory Form 6 would need the Central government to amend the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960. No decision by the Commission was reported.

sections.title: Wrong entries reported on the rolls

items.headline: New voters list in Indian state includes wrong photos and dead people
items.claim: The BBC reported that voters in villages near Patna told it the Bihar draft roll carried wrong photographs, duplicate entries and the name of a person who died more than five years earlier. It reported that in Danara village many residents were not sure officials had visited their homes.
items.response: In response to the BBC's questions, the Election Commission shared its 24 June order on conducting the SIR and a 27 July press note outlining efforts to ensure no eligible voter was "left behind". "Further, [the commission] does not take any responsibility of any other misinformation or unsubstantiated allegations being floated around by some vested interests," it added. The BBC also noted the commission has said BLOs worked "very responsibly".

items.headline: Declared Dead in Draft Electoral Roll, Bihar Voter Appears in Supreme Court
items.claim: The Wire reported that a voter from Ara, Bhojpur, who had been declared dead in the Bihar draft roll, appeared alive in the Supreme Court on 12 August 2025, produced by petitioner Yogendra Yadav. The voter told The Wire he had filled the enumeration form and that the BLO came to his house only after he complained.
items.response: Senior advocate Rakesh Dwivedi, for the Commission, called the production of the voter "drama". The bench of Justices Surya Kant and Joymalya Bagchi said there may have been an "inadvertent error", which could be rectified.

items.headline: How booth-level officers in Bihar are deleting voters arbitrarily
items.claim: Scroll reported that its analysis found 200 booths across 58 constituencies in 26 Bihar districts where between 324 and 641 names were left off the draft roll, 77,454 in all. It reported that most of the voters left off whom its team met in 10 of those booths had been marked absent or shifted though they had lived at their addresses for years, and that interviews with 17 BLOs showed no consistent procedure for deciding who was left off.
items.response: Parth Gupta, electoral registration officer for Purnia, acknowledged that one deleted voter should not have been asked for her parents' documents, and said, “Please provide her details and I will look into it.” Scroll also reported that Election Commission spokespersons and Bihar Chief Electoral Officer Vinod Singh Gunjiyal did not respond to requests for comment.

items.headline: ECI Skipped its Fraud-Busting Software, Flooding Bihar Voter Roll with Lakhs of Suspect Duplicates
items.claim: The Reporters' Collective reported that a top Commission official and four Bihar EROs confirmed to it that the Commission did not run its de-duplication software during the Bihar SIR and did not give state officials access to it. It quoted the official saying the focus was on document collection. It reported that its own earlier analysis of the final roll found 14.35 lakh suspect duplicate entries.
items.response: The Collective said the Commission and Bihar's Chief Electoral Officer did not answer its emailed questions. In person, the Chief Electoral Officer told its reporter "We cannot share this information with you" and said the Supreme Court was hearing the matter.

items.headline: Ctrl+Alive+Delete: 3 living voters in Lucknow marked 'dead' in SIR draft roll, struck off list
items.claim: Three living residents of one address in the Lucknow North constituency were listed as dead in the draft roll of 6 January 2026, The Times of India reported. All three had voted on 27 October 2025 and held acknowledgements for the enumeration forms they handed to the booth officer. At their booth 41 of 1,241 voters were marked dead.
items.quote: At this particular booth, the Booth Level Officer (BLO) declared 41 out of 1,241 voters as dead.
items.response: The Times of India reported that the Chief Electoral Officer advised everyone missing from the draft to apply on Form 6 as new voters.

items.headline: एसआईआर: यूपी में मतदाता सूची से नाम कटवाने वाले फ़ॉर्म 7 पर क्या है विवाद
items.claim: A BJP minister in the Uttar Pradesh government alleged that 9,200 bogus voters were enrolled in Varanasi South and asked for them to be checked again, BBC News Hindi reported.
items.quote: वाराणसी से यूपी सरकार में मंत्री रवींद्र जायसवाल ने आरोप लगाया है कि वाराणसी दक्षिण में 9200 फर्ज़ी मतदाता दर्ज हैं
items.response: The Varanasi District Magistrate told the media "इस मामले में बीजेपी की तरफ से शिकायत मिली है.अलग-अलग बूथों की शिकायत है. जांच के बाद उचित कार्रवाई की जाएगी."

items.headline: ‘I didn’t know my name was deleted’: Voters in Okhla on the pre-SIR ‘clean-up’
items.claim: Newslaundry reported that several voters in Delhi's Okhla constituency whose names were deleted before the SIR began said they got no notice or hearing and learnt of the deletion only when they tried to take part in the SIR. It reported that 34,644 names were deleted in Okhla during the 2026 mapping phase, against 9,170 in all of 2025.
items.response: Delhi Chief Electoral Officer Ashok Kumar said that no voter had been deleted without an inquiry and an opportunity for a hearing.

items.headline: Goa CEO says 88 of 97 voters left out after SIR have filed Form 6, applications accepted
items.claim: Goa's Chief Electoral Officer said on X that 88 of the 97 voters missing from the final roll of February 2026 had filed Form 6 and been accepted, The Pioneer reported. The cases came to light after The Indian Express reported that the Commission's software did not let verified electors be added.
items.quote: The Goa CEO's office on Thursday released the status of all 97 cases, saying 88 voters had submitted Form 6 and their applications had been accepted.

items.headline: 'Dead' on voter list, but alive: 3 Vijayapura women demand action over SIR controversy
items.claim: The Week reported that Vijayapura City MLA Basanagouda R Patil Yatnal wrote to officials on 31 August seeking the deletion of 1,054 voters, eight of whom were shown as dead on death certificates, and that three living women among them came forward on 7 October. District Electoral Officer Anandh K said no Form 7 had been filed and the certificates were found to belong to namesakes, so the inquiry was opened under the Registration of Births and Deaths Act.
items.quote: Instead, the inquiry into Yatnal's complaint was opened under the Registration of Births and Deaths Act, Anandh said.
items.response: Deputy Commissioner and District Electoral Officer Anandh K said officials were still seeking legal opinion on how to proceed. No response from the MLA was reported.

items.headline: UP Chief Electoral Officer rejects media report alleging 'mysterious' 16.18 lakh voter additions
items.claim: The Reporters' Collective reported that 16.18 lakh Form 6 applications were collected in Uttar Pradesh before the draft roll of 6 January 2026 and that their details were not published. The Chief Electoral Officer rejected the report on X, The New Indian Express reported, saying the forms were collected by booth officers during enumeration under the Commission's instructions.
items.quote: The clarification came in response to a report titled “The Mysterious 16.18 Lakh Voters Added to Uttar Pradesh’s Roll”, which questioned the collection and subsequent processing of 16.18 lakh Form-6 applications during the SIR.
items.response: The Chief Electoral Officer said "The allegations levelled in the report are not correct as these are based on faulty assumptions and are therefore categorically denied", that only Form 6s received after the draft had to go in the published list of claims, and that "There is no formula or logic for the acceptance of forms to adhere to a particular percentage."

items.headline: Final verification for 46.63L flagged voters launched
items.claim: The Hans India reported that Andhra Pradesh's Chief Electoral Officer announced a door-to-door re-check of 46,62,583 names before the final roll of 16 October. They are the 44,89,512 left off the draft and the 1,73,071 found ineligible after notices, and booth officers are to help anyone left off in error file Form 6.
items.response: The paper quoted the Chief Electoral Officer, Vivek Yadav, as saying the drive will recheck the flagged cases, and that a name found deleted by mistake is to be restored through Form 6 after verification.

items.headline: "Fraud across the 403 seats": Akhilesh Yadav threatens to release proof of SIR fraud
items.claim: The Samajwadi Party president said on 12 October 2026 that Uttar Pradesh's voter list holds lakhs of fake votes, with one person registered as many as ten times, and that the party had found such entries in several Assembly constituencies and would release the list, ANI reported.
items.quote: There are lakhs of fake votes in Uttar Pradesh. A single person has as many as ten votes registered. We have identified such fake votes in several assembly constituencies... we will release the list.

items.headline: Delhi SIR 2026: Over 2.3 lakh new voter registration applications received between August 31 and October 15
items.claim: ANI reported figures from Delhi's Chief Electoral Officer. Between the draft of 31 August and 15 October the office received 2,30,165 Form 6 applications to be added to the roll and 12,568 Form 7 objections, beside 2,12,400 Form 6 recorded up to 30 August and 51,471 Form 7 recorded earlier. Special camps were set at polling stations across Delhi on 18 and 25 October. Claims and objections close on 30 October, are to be decided by 30 November, and the final roll is due on 4 December 2026.

items.headline: Door-to-door BLO visits expected to include ‘left-out’ voters in Delhi SIR
items.claim: The Indian Express reported that Delhi's Chief Electoral Officer ordered on 14 October a special drive to find eligible electors left off the draft roll. Booth officers visiting homes to collect documents from those sent notices are also to look for electors left off in their part and help those found eligible fill in Form 6. Booth officers told the paper the instruction reached them orally or on WhatsApp and that they had seen no formal order. One registration officer's message asked them to visit every elector marked absent, shifted, dead or duplicate within seven days and take Form 6 from any found living at the address. The paper reported that the office also directed that Form 6 handed in on paper must not be refused and must be entered within two days.
items.response: The paper reported a statement from the Chief Electoral Officer's office that 26 lakh of the 33.1 lakh notices had been resolved.

items.headline: Congress alleges voter roll manipulation in UP's Pilibhit, seeks probe into SIR process
items.claim: The Uttar Pradesh Congress alleged at a press conference in Lucknow that in Pilibhit Sadar the names of 13,150 voters were changed between July and September, after the final roll of 10 April 2026, while their EPIC and serial numbers stayed the same, PTI reported. The party said 884 names of people still living there were deleted and 2,600 names of people who did not live there were added, and that the changes appeared to have been made in batches. It asked for an inquiry and said it would go to court. These are the Congress's allegations.
items.quote: If the same EPIC number is assigned to another person, the original voter may face an identity mismatch at the time of voting and be denied the right to vote,
items.response: The report carries no response. The next day The Wire reported that the Chief Electoral Officer, after an inquiry found that searching some EPIC numbers online showed other voters' details, had ordered the constituency's Electoral Registration Officer and Voter Registration Centre operator off roll duties and legal action against them.

items.headline: UP MLC Voter List: 'राम ने शर्मा को मारा', पिता का नाम- 'टक्कर मारना'; वोटर लिस्ट में अजीबोगरीब नाम
items.claim: Voter slips for the Legislative Council election in the Allahabad-Jhansi graduates' constituency, where polling was set for 23 October, carried Hindi phrases in place of electors' and fathers' names, and pictures of them spread on social media before the polling parties left, Dainik Jagran reported. On the instructions of the Chief Electoral Officer, Navdeep Rinwa, the Returning Officer, Bimal Kumar Dubey, who is Divisional Commissioner of Jhansi, had the roll checked and reported clerical errors and more than 100 duplicate names. The Bharatiya Janata Party separately complained to the Chief Electoral Officer that the roll held 4,397 duplicate electors, and that electors born between 2001 and 2005 were on it whom the party called too young to qualify. The party's Prayagraj city president put 3,163 of the duplicates in Prayagraj.
items.quote: जांच में मतदाता सूची में लिपकीय त्रुटियों के साथ ही 100 से अधिक डुप्लीकेट मतदाताओं के नाम भी सामने आए हैं।
items.response: The Returning Officer said in a press note of 17 October that no elector would be denied the vote because of a clerical error, and that an elector whose identity satisfied the presiding officer or polling officer would be allowed to vote. The report says the clerical errors found in the check were marked and corrected, and that a separate list of the duplicate names was being given to the presiding officers of the polling stations concerned, with instructions to keep a special watch on those names during the poll.

items.headline: Pilibhit Voter Roll Irregularities: FIR Against Two SDMs, Computer Operator Over 10,470 Entries
items.claim: An FIR was lodged on 22 October against the two Sub-Divisional Magistrates who had served as Pilibhit's Electoral Registration Officers and a computer operator at the constituency's Voter Registration Centre, under Section 32 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, and the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, The Wire reported. The Chief Electoral Officer's inquiry found that the operator had entered 13,779 Form 8 applications to change voters' details between 31 May and 29 August 2026, of which 10,470 were approved and 3,309 rejected, and that the office held no forms or records for any of them. The two officers were moved to district headquarters and the operator's services were ended. The District Election Officer was told to examine every Form 6 and Form 7 entry made by the same operator from 10 April to 21 October.
items.quote: No forms or records related to any of these entries were found available in the office,
items.response: The finding is the Chief Electoral Officer's own. Officials said the entries found irregular were being corrected, and the District Magistrate said the rolls of every constituency in the district would be cleaned up in a day or two.

items.headline: Six election officials removed in U.P. after SP flags voter list errors
items.claim: The Chief Electoral Officer of Uttar Pradesh, Navdeep Rinwa, took five booth level officers and a computer assistant off all roll work on 24 October and began ending their services, after an inquiry into the roll of the Azamgarh Assembly constituency (347), The Hindu reported. The Samajwadi Party had said at a press conference that one elector's name appeared ten times on that roll. The District Election Officer's report found the name 13 times in Hindi. Two of the entries had been taken up for deletion, and the other 11 belonged to 11 different people living in Azamgarh, ten of whose names and details were being corrected through Form 8. The Chief Electoral Officer ordered charge sheets and departmental proceedings against the Electoral Registration Officer of the time and two Assistant Electoral Registration Officers, with action under Section 32 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, and asked for a report on the rolls of every constituency in the district within a week.
items.quote: In response to the clerical lapses, the CEO directed the immediate removal of the responsible computer assistant and five BLOs from voter registration work.
items.response: The finding is the Chief Electoral Officer's own. His office said a further entry with the same name, in the Chauri Chaura constituency of Gorakhpur district, belonged to a different elector. The Indian Express quoted him saying the three officers would face action for negligence and laxity in supervision while the roll was prepared.

items.headline: SIR exercise: After Pilibhit, Azamgarh roll ‘errors’, UP CEO orders scrutiny of all Forms 6, 7, 8 filled by computer assistants
items.claim: The Chief Electoral Officer of Uttar Pradesh, Navdeep Rinwa, ordered on 25 October that every Form 6, Form 7 and Form 8 entered by computer assistants between the final roll of 10 April and 24 October be checked again, after the errors found in the rolls of Pilibhit and Azamgarh, The Indian Express reported. Computer assistants may no longer enter forms received on paper, which booth level officers are to digitise through the BLO App. Electoral Registration Officers are to review pending forms every day, and officials were told not to share their ERONET login IDs and passwords, were directed to study Section 32 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, which deals with breaches of official duty in preparing the roll, and were warned of strict action. The office pulled up the District Election Officers of Bulandshahr, Sitapur, Ghaziabad and Aligarh for late reports on complaints of duplicate voters circulated on social media, and directed that the draft rolls of the coming Special Summary Revision carry no duplicate entries.
items.quote: “All such forms must be digitised by Booth Level Officers (BLOs) through the BLO App,” the directive stated.
items.response: The directions are the Chief Electoral Officer's own. They followed a virtual meeting with Divisional Commissioners, District Election Officers, registration officers and computer assistants, held to prepare for the Special Summary Revision, which The Hindu dates 24 October. The Hindu reports the same directions from an official statement, says officials were warned of action under Section 32, and adds that the section provides for imprisonment of at least three months and up to two years, with a fine.

items.headline: Two suicides, BLO protests threaten to disrupt SIR in Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Rajasthan
items.claim: The Indian Express reported the deaths of two BLOs. The family of a BLO in Kannur, Kerala, alleged he was under pressure to finish by December 4, and police said a note found on a BLO in Jaipur said he faced extreme pressure from his supervisor and was told he would be suspended if he did not meet his SIR target. It also reported that revenue employees in Tamil Nadu announced a statewide boycott of SIR work over workload.
items.response: Kannur District Collector Arun K Vijayan's report indicated that the BLO was not under any work pressure. The Indian Express said its multiple calls and messages to Rajasthan CEO Naveen got no response.
actors: Federation of Revenue Associations of Tamil Nadu

items.headline: 4 deaths in a week: 2 woman assistant BLOs die of ‘heart attack’ in Gujarat amid concerns on ‘SIR work pressure’
items.claim: The Indian Express reported that two women assistant BLOs died of heart attacks in Tapi and Vadodara districts, bringing BLO deaths in Gujarat that week to four. The husband of one said she was a heart patient who had asked to be excused from BLO duty, which the Vadodara Collector disputed.
items.response: Vadodara District Collector Anil Dhameliya said, “We checked with the institute as well as with the local officials. She had not made any official request to be excused (from BLO duty)… We have learnt now that she was suffering from a heart ailment and had episodes of fainting in her institute as well.” He also said, “We have been cautious about ensuring that there is no excessive workload on the BLOs and therefore, we have appointed additional staff to assist in the process.” An unnamed government official said, “With a large workforce of over two lakh involved in the SIR work, these deaths can be termed as natural. Linking these to SIR is not justified and logical.”

items.headline: Four BLOs die amid mounting pressure during electoral revision drive in UP
items.claim: The New Indian Express reported four deaths of officers on revision duty in Uttar Pradesh that families tied to workload. They were a lekhpal supervisor in Fatehpur who died by suicide a day before his wedding, after what his family said were threats of dismissal, a teacher who collapsed on duty in Bareilly, a teacher in Gonda who died by suicide and an officer in Lucknow who had a brain haemorrhage. In Fatehpur police registered an FIR for abetment against a revenue officer and unnamed officials.
items.quote: Police have filed an FIR against senior officials on abetment charges.
items.response: The paper reported, citing unnamed sources, that the family had first named the electoral registration officer and was made to change the complaint, which the Additional Superintendent of Police, Fatehpur, denied.

items.headline: Another BLO dies by suicide, blamed SIR work pressure in heartbreaking video
items.claim: A 46-year-old assistant teacher on booth officer duty since 7 October died by suicide at home in Moradabad, police said, leaving a note to the district Basic Education Officer saying he could not meet the SIR targets, India Today reported.
items.quote: I have been working day and night but am unable to meet the SIR targets. My nights have become unbearable due to anxiety.
items.response: The District Magistrate said "Preliminary information suggests he died by suicide. His quality of work was excellent. Anganwadi employees were deployed to assist him. Both administrative and police probes are underway." The Commission extended the SIR schedule by a week the same day.

items.headline: Hathras UP BLO dies amid SIR poll row; government agrees to debate next week
items.claim: A 40-year-old assistant teacher working as a booth officer in Hathras collapsed at home and died on the way to hospital, The Telegraph reported. His family said he had been under stress since starting the work. The paper counted three booth officer deaths in Uttar Pradesh since the previous Sunday.
items.quote: A booth-level officer (BLO) in Uttar Pradesh’s Hathras district died on the way to a hospital from his home in Sikandra Rao town on Tuesday morning.
items.response: The District Magistrate called the death unfortunate, said the cause would be clear after the post-mortem, and said the administration would explore a job for the officer's wife.

items.headline: Little sleep, no pay: India's poll workers flag harsh conditions amid uproar over deaths
items.claim: The BBC reported that 10 BLOs it spoke to in Uttar Pradesh and West Bengal said they worked 14 to 15 hours a day with little rest, and that families linked the deaths of more than a dozen poll workers, by alleged suicide or heart attack, to election work stress. The BBC said it had not independently verified the causes of death. It reported BLOs saying the SIR app crashed often and that many had not been paid.
items.response: The BBC said the Commission did not answer its questions. It cited media reports of a court affidavit in which the Commission called claims linking booth officers' deaths to the revision "false, exaggerated and politically motivated".

items.headline: Elderly man dies due to cardiac arrest during SIR hearing, kin allege ‘excessive stress’
items.claim: The Indian Express reported that a 75-year-old man died of cardiac arrest, according to hospital sources, after falling ill in a queue for an SIR hearing at the Rampurhat-1 block office in Birbhum. His wife and family alleged the SIR process had caused him excessive stress and held the Election Commission responsible. It also reported that an elderly man died of cardiac arrest at an SIR hearing in Howrah the previous day.

items.headline: FIR against ECI in West Bengal over alleged suicide of elderly man due to SIR 'anxiety'
items.claim: The New Indian Express, citing PTI, reported that police in Purulia registered an FIR on a complaint by the son of an 82-year-old man who died allegedly by suicide on 29 December hours before he was due at an SIR hearing. An officer was quoted as saying the case included charges of abetment of suicide and criminal conspiracy against Election Commission officials, with no official named. The family alleged he acted out of anxiety over the SIR.

unconfirmed.headline: Fresh protest at Jantar Mantar on October 10 if CEC Kumar didn't resign: CJP leader Dipke
unconfirmed.reason: The source never mentions the SIR, only the demand for the Chief Election Commissioner's resignation, so it is outside this page.
